+// Entire CLI plugin for OpenCode
+// Auto-generated by `entire enable --agent opencode`
+// Do not edit manually — changes will be overwritten on next install.
+// Requires Bun runtime (used by OpenCode's plugin system for loading ESM plugins).
+import type { Plugin } from "@opencode-ai/plugin"
+
+export const EntirePlugin: Plugin = async ({ client, directory, $ }) => {
+  const ENTIRE_CMD = "__ENTIRE_CMD__"
+  // Store transcripts outside the repo (matches Go SanitizePathForOpenCode).
+  const home = Bun.env.HOME ?? ""
+  const sanitized = directory.replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9]/g, "-")
+  const transcriptDir = `${home}/.opencode/sessions/entire/${sanitized}`
+  const seenUserMessages = new Set<string>()
+
+  // In-memory stores — used to write transcripts without relying on the SDK API,
+  // which may be unavailable during shutdown.
+  // messageStore: keyed by message ID, stores message metadata (role, time, tokens, etc.)
+  const messageStore = new Map<string, any>()
+  // partStore: keyed by message ID, stores accumulated parts from message.part.updated events
+  const partStore = new Map<string, any[]>()
+  let currentSessionID: string | null = null
+
+  // Ensure transcript directory exists
+  await $`mkdir -p ${transcriptDir}`.quiet().nothrow()
+
+  /**
+   * Pipe JSON payload to an entire hooks command.
+   * Errors are logged but never thrown — plugin failures must not crash OpenCode.
+   */
+  async function callHook(hookName: string, payload: Record<string, unknown>) {
+    try {
+      const json = JSON.stringify(payload)
+      await $`echo ${json} | ${ENTIRE_CMD} hooks opencode ${hookName}`.quiet().nothrow()
+    } catch {
+      // Silently ignore — plugin failures must not crash OpenCode
+    }
+  }

Because OpenCode is expected to integrate via its own plugin (calling `entire hooks ...`), this agent does not install or manage hooks; the setup flow is updated so `entire enable` can succeed for such agents.\r\n\r\n## Changes\r\n\r\n- **New agent: OpenCode** (`cmd/entire/cli/agent/opencode/`)\r\n  - Implements the `Agent` interface: detection, session ID transform, session dir resolution, protected dirs (`.opencode`), and resume command.\r\n  - `SupportsHooks()` returns `false`; hook input parsing is unimplemented (returns a clear error if used).\r\n  - Session read/write is implemented as a passthrough of OpenCode’s on-disk format so future hook/plugin integration can be added without changing this contract.\r\n\r\n- **Setup behavior**\r\n  - Agents that do not support hooks (e.g. OpenCode) can complete `entire enable` without installing hooks. Entire’s git hooks and strategy setup still run; only agent-specific hook installation is skipped.\r\n  - Message when no hooks are installed is updated to: “Hooks for … already installed or managed externally” so it’s accurate for both “already installed” and “managed by the agent/plugin elsewhere.”\r\n\r\n- **Registration**\r\n  - OpenCode is registered in the agent registry and wired in `config.go` and `hooks_cmd.go` so it is discoverable and usable when OpenCode (or its plugin) invokes the CLI.\r\n\r\n## Testing\r\n\r\n- `mise run test` (unit tests including new registry test for `opencode`).\r\n- Manual: `entire enable` in a repo with `.opencode/` or `opencode.json` completes successfully and does not require hook support.","comments":["Thanks for this! {"body":"Closes #245\nCloses #266\nRelates to #281\n\n## Summary\n\nAdds two new AI coding agent integrations to the Entire CLI: **OpenCode** and **Codex CLI**. Both agents support full session checkpointing via hooks — capturing transcripts, file changes, prompts, and metadata on shadow branches.\n\nAs part of this work, **duplicated framework code was extracted into a shared commit pipeline** (\"$(hooks_common_session.go)\"), directly addressing issue #281's goal of separating framework from agent-specific logic. The three agent handlers (Codex, OpenCode, Gemini) that previously duplicated ~250 lines of commit logic are now thin wrappers calling a shared \"$(commitAgentSession())\" function.\n\n**~3,000 lines across 16 files** (all new code from main's perspective).\n\n---\n\n### Framework Extraction (addresses #281)\n\nThe shared \"$(hooks_common_session.go)\" consolidates duplicated logic from Codex, OpenCode, and Gemini handlers:\n\n| Extracted Function | Replaces | Purpose |\n|---|---|---|\n| \"$(commitAgentSession())\" | \"$(commitCodexSession)\", \"$(commitOpenCodeSession)\", \"$(commitGeminiSession)\" | Core commit pipeline: load state → detect changes → save via strategy |\n| \"$(createContextFile())\" | \"$(createContextFileForCodex)\", \"$(createContextFileForOpenCode)\", \"$(createContextFileForGemini)\" | Unified context.md generation (single + multi-prompt) |\n| \"$(transitionSessionTurnEnd())\" | Was in Claude Code handlers, used by all agents | Session phase state machine transition |\n| \"$(logFileChanges())\" | Was in Gemini handlers, used by all agents | Stderr logging of modified/new/deleted files |\n\nEach agent handler is now a thin wrapper that populates an \"$(agentCommitContext)\" struct:\n- **Codex**: provides transcript-extracted modified files, single prompt\n- **OpenCode**: sets \"$(useGitStatusForModified: true)\" (no transcript parsing), single prompt\n- **Gemini**: adds token usage calculation, multi-prompt array, transcript step tracking\n\nThis reduces the barrier for adding new agents — a new handler only needs to populate the context struct and call \"$(commitAgentSession())\".\n\n**Not yet extracted** (future #281 work): Claude Code's \"$(commitWithMetadata)\" has unique subagent/summarization/incremental-checkpoint logic that requires its own pattern. The \"$(Agent)\" interface itself is also unchanged — broader interface refactoring is deferred to the core team per #281.\n\n---\n\n### OpenCode Agent\n- TypeScript plugin system: generates \"$(.opencode/plugins/entire.ts)\" that subscribes to \"$(session.created)\" and \"$(session.status)\" (busy/idle) events via BunShell\n- **3 hooks**: \"$(session-created)\" (SessionStart), \"$(session-busy)\" (per-turn state capture), \"$(session-idle)\" (Stop/checkpoint)\n- Per-turn pre-prompt state capture via \"$(session-busy)\" hook — captures untracked files before agent starts each turn for accurate new-file detection\n- File change detection via git status with pre-prompt untracked baseline (OpenCode sessions are opaque JSON — no transcript-based file extraction possible)\n- Session storage: reads from XDG data directory (\"$(~/.local/share/opencode/storage/session/)\")\n- Recursive session file discovery via \"$(filepath.WalkDir)\" (OpenCode nests sessions under \"$(\u003cprojectID\u003e/)\" subdirectories)\n\n### Codex CLI Agent\n- TOML-based notify hook: installs \"$(notify = [\"entire\", \"hooks\", \"codex\", \"agent-turn-complete\"])\" in \"$(.codex/config.toml)\"\n- Parses Codex JSONL rollout transcripts for file change extraction (\"$(file_change)\", \"$(function_call)\", \"$(event_msg/patch_apply_begin)\" items)\n- **Codex sends notify payload via argv (not stdin)** — handler reads from last positional argument via \"$(GetCurrentHookArgs())\"\n- Post-turn state capture — captures untracked files after each turn completes as structure)\n- Session storage: reads from \"$(~/.codex/sessions/)\" (respects \"$(CODEX_HOME)\" env var)\n- Local dev mode resolves project path at write-time via \"$(paths.RepoRoot())\" (Codex registry entries for both agents in \"$(hook_registry.go)\"\n- \"$(currentHookArgs)\" + \"$(GetCurrentHookArgs())\" for agents that pass payloads via positional args\n- \"$(fileExistsAndIsRegular())\" helper to distinguish files from directories\n\n---\n\n### Key Implementation Details\n\n**Codex argv payload handling:**\nCodex's Rust source (\"$(user_notification.rs)\") calls \"$(command.arg(notify_payload))\" with \"$(stdin(Stdio::null()))\". The hook registry captures positional args via \"$(cobra.ArbitraryArgs)\" and stores them in \"$(currentHookArgs)\". The handler reads from \"$(args[len(args)-1])\" when available, falling back to stdin.\n\n**OpenCode session-busy hook:**\nOpenCode fires \"$(session.status)\" with \"$(type: \"busy\")\" when the agent starts processing each turn. The TypeScript plugin pipes this to \"$(entire hooks opencode session-busy)\", which calls \"$(CapturePrePromptState(sessionID, \"\"))\" to snapshot untracked files before the agent modifies anything. The subsequent \"$(session-idle)\" handler uses \"$(commitAgentSession())\" with \"$(useGitStatusForModified: true)\".\n\n**Codex post-turn state capture (workaround):**\nCodex only exposes \"$(AfterAgent)\" and \"$(AfterToolUse)\" hooks — no \"before turn\" event exists. As a workaround, \"$(handleCodexAgentTurnComplete)\" captures state after each turn completes (\"$(CapturePrePromptState)\" at the end), which serves as the baseline for the next turn's \"$(DetectFileChanges)\".\n\n**File existence checks:**\n\"$(fileExistsAndIsRegular())\" replaces \"$(fileExists())\" for transcript path validation. # OpenCode: Overview

Based on the provided web content, here's what can be determined about OpenCode:

## Core Identity

OpenCode is **"an open source agent that helps you write code in your terminal, IDE, or desktop."** The project has achieved significant traction with 100K GitHub stars, 700 contributors, and serves 2.5M monthly developers.

## Key Features

The platform offers:
- **LSP Integration**: Automatically loads appropriate Language Server Protocols for the LLM
- **Multi-session capability**: Run multiple agents simultaneously on the same project
- **Session sharing**: Generate links to sessions for debugging and reference
- **Model flexibility**: Support for 75+ LLM providers through Models.dev, including local models
- **Authentication options**: GitHub Copilot, ChatGPT Plus/Pro, and any compatible AI provider
- **Multi-platform availability**: Terminal interface, desktop app (beta for macOS, Windows, Linux), and IDE extensions

## Privacy & Licensing

The documentation emphasizes that "OpenCode does not store any of your code or context data," making it suitable for privacy-sensitive environments. The project is open source, though the specific license isn't detailed in this excerpt.

## Additional Offerings

**Zen** is a complementary service providing "handpicked set of AI models that OpenCode has tested and benchmarked specifically for coding agents."

**Note**: The provided content is primarily marketing material. Detailed documentation on architecture, hook systems, plugins, configuration, and API specifics would require accessing the `/docs` section.

   130→+    } catch {
   131→+      // API unavailable (likely shutting down) — fall back to in-memory stores
   132→+      return writeTranscriptFromMemory(sessionID)
   133→+    }
   134→+  }
   135→+
   136→+  return {
   137→+    event: async ({ event }) => {
   138→+      switch (event.type) {
   139→+        case "session.created": {
   140→+          const session = (event as any).properties?.info
   141→+          if (!session?.id) break
   142→+          currentSessionID = session.id
   143→+          await callHook("session-start", {
   144→+            session_id: session.id,
   145→+            transcript_path: `${transcriptDir}/${session.id}.json`,
   146→+          })
   147→+          break
   148→+        }
   149→+
   150→+        case "message.updated": {
   151→+          const msg = (event as any).properties?.info
   152→+          if (!msg) break
   153→+          // Store message metadata (role, time, tokens, etc.)
   154→+          // Content is NOT on the message — it arrives via message.part.updated events.
   155→+          messageStore.set(msg.id, msg)
   156→+          break
   157→+        }
   158→+
   159→+        case "message.part.updated": {
   160→+          const part = (event as any).properties?.part
   161→+          if (!part?.messageID) break
   162→+
   163→+          // Accumulate parts per message
   164→+          const existing = partStore.get(part.messageID) ?? []
   165→+          // Replace existing part with same id, or append new one
   166→+          const idx = existing.findIndex((p: any) => p.id === part.id)
   167→+          if (idx >= 0) {
   168→+            existing[idx] = part
   169→+          } else {
   170→+            existing.push(part)
   171→+          }
   172→+          partStore.set(part.messageID, existing)
   173→+
   174→+          // Fire turn-start on the first text part of a new user message
   175→+          const msg = messageStore.get(part.messageID)
   176→+          if (msg?.role === "user" && part.type === "text" && !seenUserMessages.has(msg.id)) {
   177→+            seenUserMessages.add(msg.id)
   178→+            const sessionID = msg.sessionID ?? currentSessionID
   179→+            if (sessionID) {
   180→+              await callHook("turn-start", {
   181→+                session_id: sessionID,
   182→+                transcript_path: `${transcriptDir}/${sessionID}.json`,
   183→+                prompt: part.text ?? "",
   184→+              })
   185→+            }
   186→+          }
   187→+          break
   188→+        }
   189→+
   190→+        case "session.idle": {
   191→+          const sessionID = (event as any).properties?.sessionID
   192→+          if (!sessionID) break
   193→+          const transcriptPath = await writeTranscriptWithFallback(sessionID)
   194→+          await callHook("turn-end", {
   195→+            session_id: sessionID,
   196→+            transcript_path: transcriptPath,
   197→+          })
   198→+          break
   199→+        }
   200→+
   201→+        case "session.compacted": {
   202→+          const sessionID = (event as any).properties?.sessionID
   203→+          if (!sessionID) break
   204→+          await callHook("compaction", {
   205→+            session_id: sessionID,
   206→+            transcript_path: `${transcriptDir}/${sessionID}.json`,
   207→+          })
   208→+          break
   209→+        }
   210→+
   211→+        case "session.deleted": {
   212→+          const session = (event as any).properties?.info
   213→+          if (!session?.id) break
   214→+          // Write final transcript before signaling session end
   215→+          if (messageStore.size > 0) {
   216→+            await writeTranscriptFromMemory(session.id)
   217→+          }
   218→+          seenUserMessages.clear()
   219→+          messageStore.clear()
   220→+          partStore.clear()
   221→+          currentSessionID = null
   222→+          await callHook("session-end", {
   223→+            session_id: session.id,
   224→+            transcript_path: `${transcriptDir}/${session.id}.json`,
   225→+          })
   226→+          break
   227→+        }
   228→+      }
   229→+    },
   230→+  }
   231→+}

   261→+	entireMarker = "Auto-generated by `entire enable --agent opencode`"
   262→+)

   264→+// getPluginPath returns the absolute path to the plugin file.
   265→+func getPluginPath() (string, error) {
   266→+	repoRoot, err := paths.RepoRoot()
   267→+	if err != nil {
   268→+		// Fallback to CWD if not in a git repo (e.g., during tests)
   269→+		//nolint:forbidigo // Intentional fallback when RepoRoot() fails (tests run outside git repos)
   270→+		repoRoot, err = os.Getwd()
   271→+		if err != nil {
   272→+			return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to get current directory: %w", err)
   273→+		}
   274→+	}
   275→+	return filepath.Join(repoRoot, ".opencode", pluginDirName, pluginFileName), nil
   276→+}
   277→+
   278→+// InstallHooks writes the Entire plugin file to .opencode/plugins/entire.ts.
   279→+// Returns 1 if the plugin was installed, 0 if already present (idempotent).
   280→+func (a *OpenCodeAgent) InstallHooks(localDev bool, force bool) (int, error) {
   281→+	pluginPath, err := getPluginPath()
   282→+	if err != nil {
   283→+		return 0, err
   284→+	}
   285→+
   286→+	// Check if already installed (idempotent) unless force
   287→+	if !force {
   288→+		if _, err := os.Stat(pluginPath); err == nil {
   289→+			data, readErr := os.ReadFile(pluginPath) //nolint:gosec // Path constructed from repo root
   290→+			if readErr == nil && strings.Contains(string(data), entireMarker) {
   291→+				return 0, nil // Already installed
   292→+			}
   293→+		}
   294→+	}
   295→+
   296→+	// Build the command prefix
   297→+	var cmdPrefix string
   298→+	if localDev {
   299→+		cmdPrefix = "go run ${OPENCODE_PROJECT_DIR}/cmd/entire/main.go"
   300→+	} else {
   301→+		cmdPrefix = "entire"
   302→+	}
   303→+
   304→+	// Generate plugin content from template
   305→+	content := strings.ReplaceAll(pluginTemplate, entireCmdPlaceholder, cmdPrefix)
   306→+
   307→+	// Ensure directory exists
   308→+	pluginDir := filepath.Dir(pluginPath)
   309→+	//nolint:gosec // G301: Plugin directory needs standard permissions
   310→+	if err := os.MkdirAll(pluginDir, 0o755); err != nil {
   311→+		return 0, fmt.Errorf("failed to create plugin directory: %w", err)
   312→+	}
   313→+
   314→+	// Write plugin file
   315→+	//nolint:gosec // G306: Plugin file needs standard permissions for OpenCode to read
   316→+	if err := os.WriteFile(pluginPath, []byte(content), 0o644); err != nil {
   317→+		return 0, fmt.Errorf("failed to write plugin file: %w", err)
   318→+	}
   319→+
   320→+	return 1, nil
   321→+}
   322→+
   323→+// UninstallHooks removes the Entire plugin file.
   324→+func (a *OpenCodeAgent) UninstallHooks() error {
   325→+	pluginPath, err := getPluginPath()
   326→+	if err != nil {
   327→+		return err
   328→+	}
   329→+
   330→+	if err := os.Remove(pluginPath); err != nil && !os.IsNotExist(err) {
   331→+		return fmt.Errorf("failed to remove plugin file: %w", err)
   332→+	}
   333→+
   334→+	return nil
   335→+}
   336→+
   337→+// AreHooksInstalled checks if the Entire plugin file exists and contains the marker.
   338→+func (a *OpenCodeAgent) AreHooksInstalled() bool {
   339→+	pluginPath, err := getPluginPath()
   340→+	if err != nil {
   341→+		return false
   342→+	}
   343→+
   344→+	data, err := os.ReadFile(pluginPath) //nolint:gosec // Path constructed from repo root
   345→+	if err != nil {
   346→+		return false
   347→+	}
   348→+
   349→+	return strings.Contains(string(data), entireMarker)
   350→+}
   351→+
   352→+// GetSupportedHooks returns the normalized lifecycle events this agent supports.
   353→+// OpenCode's native hooks map to standard agent lifecycle events:
   354→+//   - session-start → HookSessionStart
   355→+//   - session-end   → HookSessionEnd
   356→+//   - turn-start    → HookUserPromptSubmit (user prompt triggers a turn)
   357→+//   - turn-end      → HookStop (agent response complete)
   358→+//
   359→+// Note: HookNames() returns 5 hooks (including "compaction"), but GetSupportedHooks()
   360→+// returns only 4. The "compaction" hook is OpenCode-specific with no standard HookType
   361→+// mapping — it is handled via ParseHookEvent but not advertised as a standard lifecycle event.
   362→+func (a *OpenCodeAgent) GetSupportedHooks() []agent.HookType {
   363→+	return []agent.HookType{
   364→+		agent.HookSessionStart,
   365→+		agent.HookSessionEnd,
   366→+		agent.HookUserPromptSubmit,
   367→+		agent.HookStop,
   368→+	}
   369→+}

# OpenCode Architecture & Integration Documentation

Based on the provided web content, here's what I found about OpenCode's technical architecture:

## Core Architecture

OpenCode is a **Go-based CLI application** built with:
- **Bubble Tea** for the Terminal User Interface (TUI)
- **SQLite database** for persistent storage of conversations and sessions
- **Language Server Protocol (LSP)** support for code intelligence

## AI Provider Support

The system integrates with multiple AI providers through a modular provider system:
- OpenAI (GPT-4.1, GPT-4.5, GPT-4o, O1/O3 families)
- Anthropic Claude (3.5/3.7 Sonnet, 4 variants)
- Google Gemini (2.5, 2.0 Flash)
- GitHub Copilot
- AWS Bedrock
- Groq
- Azure OpenAI
- Google Cloud VertexAI
- OpenRouter

## Tool Integration System

The AI assistant has access to tools enabling:
- Command execution capabilities
- File searching functionality
- Code modification abilities
- "Tool integration" for external capabilities

The configuration supports **MCP (Model Context Protocol) Servers** with stdio-type connections, allowing external tool integration through standardized interfaces.

## Configuration System

Configuration supports:
- Provider-specific API keys via environment variables
- Agent-level settings (model selection, max tokens)
- LSP configuration per language
- Custom shell path and arguments
- "Auto compact feature" for context window management (auto-summarizes conversations at 95% capacity)

## Storage & Sessions

- Persistent SQLite-based storage for conversations
- Session management with file change tracking
- Configurable data directory

**Note:** The documentation excerpt doesn't detail the internal plugin API, session event schemas, or transcript format specifications—these implementation details aren't covered in the provided content.

# OpenCode Plugin System Overview

## Plugin Architecture

Plugins are JavaScript/TypeScript modules that extend OpenCode functionality. Each plugin exports a function receiving a context object and returning a hooks object.

**Basic Structure:**
```javascript
export const MyPlugin = async ({ project, client, $, directory, worktree }) => {
  return {
    // Hook implementations
  }
}
```

**Context Parameters:**
- `project`: Current project information
- `client`: OpenCode SDK client for AI interaction
- `$`: Bun's shell API for command execution
- `directory`: Current working directory
- `worktree`: Git worktree path

## Plugin Loading

### Installation Methods

1. **Local files**: Place in `.opencode/plugins/` (project) or `~/.config/opencode/plugins/` (global)
2. **npm packages**: Specify in config via `"plugin"` array

### Load Order
1. Global config
2. Project config
3. Global plugin directory
4. Project plugin directory

npm packages auto-install via Bun to `~/.cache/opencode/node_modules/`.

## Available Events

**Command**: `command.executed`

**File**: `file.edited`, `file.watcher.updated`

**Installation**: `installation.updated`

**LSP**: `lsp.client.diagnostics`, `lsp.updated`

**Message**: `message.part.removed`, `message.part.updated`, `message.removed`, `message.updated`

**Permission**: `permission.asked`, `permission.replied`

**Server**: `server.connected`

**Session**: `session.created`, `session.compacted`, `session.deleted`, `session.diff`, `session.error`, `session.idle`, `session.status`, `session.updated`

**Todo**: `todo.updated`

**Shell**: `shell.env`

**Tool**: `tool.execute.after`, `tool.execute.before`

**TUI**: `tui.prompt.append`, `tui.command.execute`, `tui.toast.show`

## Key API Methods

**Logging:**
```typescript
await client.app.log({
  body: {
    service: "plugin-name",
    level: "info|debug|warn|error",
    message: "text",
    extra: {}
  }
})
```

## Custom Tools

Plugins can define tools using the `tool` helper:

```typescript
import { type Plugin, tool } from "@opencode-ai/plugin"

export const CustomToolsPlugin: Plugin = async (ctx) => {
  return {
    tool: {
      mytool: tool({
        description: "Tool description",
        args: { foo: tool.schema.string() },
        async execute(args, context) {
          return "result"
        }
      })
    }
  }
}
```

## Dependencies

Local plugins can use external packages by adding `.opencode/package.json`:

```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "package-name": "^version"
  }
}
```

OpenCode runs `bun install` at startup.

## Notable Hook Examples

**Tool execution filtering:**
```javascript
"tool.execute.before": async (input, output) => {
  if (input.tool === "bash") {
    // Modify output.args
  }
}
```

**Session compaction customization:**
```javascript
"experimental.session.compacting": async (input, output) => {
  output.context.push("## Custom context")
  // OR replace entirely: output.prompt = "..."
}
```

**Environment injection:**
```javascript
"shell.env": async (input, output) => {
  output.env.MY_VAR = "value"
}
```

## TypeScript Support

Import type definitions:
```typescript
import type { Plugin } from "@opencode-ai/plugin"

export const MyPlugin: Plugin = async (ctx) => {
  // Type-safe implementation
}
```

   598→+// ParseHookEvent translates OpenCode hook calls into normalized lifecycle events.
   599→+func (a *OpenCodeAgent) ParseHookEvent(hookName string, stdin io.Reader) (*agent.Event, error) {
   600→+	switch hookName {
   601→+	case HookNameSessionStart:
   602→+		raw, err := agent.ReadAndParseHookInput[sessionInfoRaw](stdin)
   603→+		if err != nil {
   604→+			return nil, err
   605→+		}
   606→+		return &agent.Event{
   607→+			Type:       agent.SessionStart,
   608→+			SessionID:  raw.SessionID,
   609→+			SessionRef: raw.TranscriptPath,
   610→+			Timestamp:  time.Now(),
   611→+		}, nil
   612→+
   613→+	case HookNameTurnStart:
   614→+		raw, err := agent.ReadAndParseHookInput[turnStartRaw](stdin)
   615→+		if err != nil {
   616→+			return nil, err
   617→+		}
   618→+		return &agent.Event{
   619→+			Type:       agent.TurnStart,
   620→+			SessionID:  raw.SessionID,
   621→+			SessionRef: raw.TranscriptPath,
   622→+			Prompt:     raw.Prompt,
   623→+			Timestamp:  time.Now(),
   624→+		}, nil
   625→+
   626→+	case HookNameTurnEnd:
   627→+		raw, err := agent.ReadAndParseHookInput[sessionInfoRaw](stdin)
   628→+		if err != nil {
   629→+			return nil, err
   630→+		}
   631→+		return &agent.Event{
   632→+			Type:       agent.TurnEnd,
   633→+			SessionID:  raw.SessionID,
   634→+			SessionRef: raw.TranscriptPath,
   635→+			Timestamp:  time.Now(),
   636→+		}, nil
   637→+
   638→+	case HookNameCompaction:
   639→+		raw, err := agent.ReadAndParseHookInput[sessionInfoRaw](stdin)
   640→+		if err != nil {
   641→+			return nil, err
   642→+		}
   643→+		return &agent.Event{
   644→+			Type:       agent.Compaction,
   645→+			SessionID:  raw.SessionID,
   646→+			SessionRef: raw.TranscriptPath,
   647→+			Timestamp:  time.Now(),
   648→+		}, nil
   649→+
   650→+	case HookNameSessionEnd:
   651→+		raw, err := agent.ReadAndParseHookInput[sessionInfoRaw](stdin)
   652→+		if err != nil {
   653→+			return nil, err
   654→+		}
   655→+		return &agent.Event{
   656→+			Type:       agent.SessionEnd,
   657→+			SessionID:  raw.SessionID,
   658→+			SessionRef: raw.TranscriptPath,
   659→+			Timestamp:  time.Now(),
   660→+		}, nil
   661→+
   662→+	default:
   663→+		return nil, nil //nolint:nilnil // nil event = no lifecycle action for unknown hooks
   664→+	}
   665→+}

   929→+func (a *OpenCodeAgent) ChunkTranscript(content []byte, maxSize int) ([][]byte, error) {
   930→+	// OpenCode uses JSON format (like Gemini). Parse and split by messages.
   931→+	if len(content) <= maxSize {
   932→+		return [][]byte{content}, nil
   933→+	}
   934→+
   935→+	var transcript Transcript
   936→+	if err := json.Unmarshal(content, &transcript); err != nil {
   937→+		// Fallback to JSONL chunking if not valid JSON
   938→+		chunks, chunkErr := agent.ChunkJSONL(content, maxSize)
   939→+		if chunkErr != nil {
   940→+			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to chunk transcript as JSONL: %w", chunkErr)
   941→+		}
   942→+		return chunks, nil
   943→+	}
   944→+
   945→+	if len(transcript.Messages) == 0 {
   946→+		return [][]byte{content}, nil
   947→+	}
   948→+
   949→+	// Pre-marshal each message to avoid O(n²) re-serialization.
   950→+	// Track running size and split at chunk boundaries (same approach as Gemini).
   951→+	var chunks [][]byte
   952→+	var currentMessages []Message
   953→+	baseSize := len(fmt.Sprintf(`{"session_id":%q,"messages":[]}`, transcript.SessionID))
   954→+	currentSize := baseSize
   955→+
   956→+	for _, msg := range transcript.Messages {
   957→+		msgBytes, err := json.Marshal(msg)
   958→+		if err != nil {
   959→+			continue // Skip messages that fail to marshal
   960→+		}
   961→+		msgSize := len(msgBytes) + 1 // +1 for comma separator
   962→+
   963→+		if currentSize+msgSize > maxSize && len(currentMessages) > 0 {
   964→+			// Save current chunk
   965→+			chunkData, marshalErr := json.Marshal(Transcript{
   966→+				SessionID: transcript.SessionID,
   967→+				Messages:  currentMessages,
   968→+			})
   969→+			if marshalErr != nil {
   970→+				return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal transcript chunk: %w", marshalErr)
   971→+			}
   972→+			chunks = append(chunks, chunkData)
   973→+
   974→+			// Start new chunk
   975→+			currentMessages = nil
   976→+			currentSize = baseSize
   977→+		}
   978→+
   979→+		currentMessages = append(currentMessages, msg)
   980→+		currentSize += msgSize
   981→+	}
   982→+
   983→+	// Save remaining messages
   984→+	if len(currentMessages) > 0 {
   985→+		chunkData, err := json.Marshal(Transcript{
   986→+			SessionID: transcript.SessionID,
   987→+			Messages:  currentMessages,
   988→+		})
   989→+		if err != nil {
   990→+			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal final transcript chunk: %w", err)
   991→+		}
   992→+		chunks = append(chunks, chunkData)
   993→+	}
   994→+
   995→+	return chunks, nil
   996→+}

  1067→+func (a *OpenCodeAgent) ReadSession(input *agent.HookInput) (*agent.AgentSession, error) {

  1085→+		SessionID:     input.SessionID,
  1086→+		SessionRef:    input.SessionRef,
  1087→+		NativeData:    data,
  1088→+		ModifiedFiles: modifiedFiles,
  1089→+	}, nil
  1090→+}
  1091→+
  1092→+func (a *OpenCodeAgent) WriteSession(session *agent.AgentSession) error {
  1093→+	if session == nil {
  1094→+		return errors.New("nil session")
  1095→+	}
  1096→+	if session.SessionRef == "" {
  1097→+		return errors.New("no session ref to write to")
  1098→+	}
  1099→+	if len(session.NativeData) == 0 {
  1100→+		return errors.New("no session data to write")
  1101→+	}
  1102→+	dir := filepath.Dir(session.SessionRef)
  1103→+	//nolint:gosec // G301: Session directory needs standard permissions
  1104→+	if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o755); err != nil {
  1105→+		return fmt.Errorf("failed to create session directory: %w", err)
  1106→+	}
  1107→+	if err := os.WriteFile(session.SessionRef, session.NativeData, 0o600); err != nil {
  1108→+		return fmt.Errorf("failed to write session data: %w", err)
  1109→+	}
  1110→+	return nil
  1111→+}
  1112→+
  1113→+func (a *OpenCodeAgent) FormatResumeCommand(sessionID string) string {
  1114→+	return "opencode --session " + sessionID
  1115→+}

  1117→+// nonAlphanumericRegex matches any non-alphanumeric character.
  1118→+var nonAlphanumericRegex = regexp.MustCompile(`[^a-zA-Z0-9]`)
  1119→+
  1120→+// SanitizePathForOpenCode converts a path to a safe directory name.
  1121→+// Replaces any non-alphanumeric character with a dash (same approach as Claude/Gemini).
  1122→+func SanitizePathForOpenCode(path string) string {
  1123→+	return nonAlphanumericRegex.ReplaceAllString(path, "-")
  1124→+}

  1146→+package opencode

  1160→+	_ agent.TokenCalculator    = (*OpenCodeAgent)(nil)

  1163→+// ParseTranscript parses raw JSON content into a transcript structure.
  1164→+func ParseTranscript(data []byte) (*Transcript, error) {
  1165→+	var t Transcript
  1166→+	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &t); err != nil {
  1167→+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to parse opencode transcript: %w", err)
  1168→+	}
  1169→+	return &t, nil
  1170→+}
  1171→+
  1172→+// parseTranscriptFile reads and parses a transcript JSON file.
  1173→+func parseTranscriptFile(path string) (*Transcript, error) {
  1174→+	data, err := os.ReadFile(path) //nolint:gosec // Path from agent hook
  1175→+	if err != nil {
  1176→+		return nil, err //nolint:wrapcheck // Callers check os.IsNotExist on this error
  1177→+	}
  1178→+	var t Transcript
  1179→+	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &t); err != nil {
  1180→+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to parse opencode transcript: %w", err)
  1181→+	}
  1182→+	return &t, nil
  1183→+}
  1184→+
  1185→+// GetTranscriptPosition returns the number of messages in the transcript.
  1186→+func (a *OpenCodeAgent) GetTranscriptPosition(path string) (int, error) {
  1187→+	t, err := parseTranscriptFile(path)
  1188→+	if err != nil {
  1189→+		if os.IsNotExist(err) {
  1190→+			return 0, nil
  1191→+		}
  1192→+		return 0, err
  1193→+	}
  1194→+	return len(t.Messages), nil
  1195→+}
  1196→+
  1197→+// ExtractModifiedFilesFromOffset extracts files modified by tool calls from the given message offset.
  1198→+func (a *OpenCodeAgent) ExtractModifiedFilesFromOffset(path string, startOffset int) ([]string, int, error) {
  1199→+	t, err := parseTranscriptFile(path)
  1200→+	if err != nil {
  1201→+		if os.IsNotExist(err) {
  1202→+			return nil, 0, nil
  1203→+		}
  1204→+		return nil, 0, err
  1205→+	}
  1206→+
  1207→+	seen := make(map[string]bool)
  1208→+	var files []string
  1209→+
  1210→+	for i := startOffset; i < len(t.Messages); i++ {
  1211→+		msg := t.Messages[i]
  1212→+		if msg.Role != roleAssistant {
  1213→+			continue
  1214→+		}
  1215→+		for _, part := range msg.Parts {
  1216→+			if part.Type != "tool" || part.State == nil {
  1217→+				continue
  1218→+			}
  1219→+			if !slices.Contains(FileModificationTools, part.Tool) {
  1220→+				continue
  1221→+			}
  1222→+			filePath := extractFilePathFromInput(part.State.Input)
  1223→+			if filePath != "" && !seen[filePath] {
  1224→+				seen[filePath] = true
  1225→+				files = append(files, filePath)
  1226→+			}
  1227→+		}
  1228→+	}
  1229→+
  1230→+	return files, len(t.Messages), nil
  1231→+}
  1232→+
  1233→+// ExtractModifiedFiles extracts modified file paths from raw transcript bytes.
  1234→+// This is the bytes-based equivalent of ExtractModifiedFilesFromOffset, used by ReadSession.
  1235→+func ExtractModifiedFiles(data []byte) ([]string, error) {
  1236→+	t, err := ParseTranscript(data)
  1237→+	if err != nil {
  1238→+		return nil, err
  1239→+	}
  1240→+
  1241→+	seen := make(map[string]bool)
  1242→+	var files []string
  1243→+
  1244→+	for _, msg := range t.Messages {
  1245→+		if msg.Role != roleAssistant {
  1246→+			continue
  1247→+		}
  1248→+		for _, part := range msg.Parts {
  1249→+			if part.Type != "tool" || part.State == nil {
  1250→+				continue
  1251→+			}
  1252→+			if !slices.Contains(FileModificationTools, part.Tool) {
  1253→+				continue
  1254→+			}
  1255→+			filePath := extractFilePathFromInput(part.State.Input)
  1256→+			if filePath != "" && !seen[filePath] {
  1257→+				seen[filePath] = true
  1258→+				files = append(files, filePath)
  1259→+			}
  1260→+		}
  1261→+	}
  1262→+
  1263→+	return files, nil
  1264→+}
  1265→+
  1266→+// extractFilePathFromInput extracts the file path from a tool's input map.
  1267→+func extractFilePathFromInput(input map[string]interface{}) string {
  1268→+	for _, key := range []string{"file_path", "path", "file", "filename"} {
  1269→+		if v, ok := input[key]; ok {
  1270→+			if s, ok := v.(string); ok && s != "" {
  1271→+				return s
  1272→+			}
  1273→+		}
  1274→+	}
  1275→+	return ""
  1276→+}
  1277→+
  1278→+// ExtractPrompts extracts user prompt strings from the transcript starting at the given offset.
  1279→+func (a *OpenCodeAgent) ExtractPrompts(sessionRef string, fromOffset int) ([]string, error) {
  1280→+	t, err := parseTranscriptFile(sessionRef)
  1281→+	if err != nil {
  1282→+		if os.IsNotExist(err) {
  1283→+			return nil, nil
  1284→+		}
  1285→+		return nil, err
  1286→+	}
  1287→+
  1288→+	var prompts []string
  1289→+	for i := fromOffset; i < len(t.Messages); i++ {
  1290→+		msg := t.Messages[i]
  1291→+		if msg.Role == roleUser && msg.Content != "" {
  1292→+			prompts = append(prompts, msg.Content)
  1293→+		}
  1294→+	}
  1295→+
  1296→+	return prompts, nil
  1297→+}
  1298→+
  1299→+// ExtractSummary extracts the last assistant message content as a summary.
  1300→+func (a *OpenCodeAgent) ExtractSummary(sessionRef string) (string, error) {
  1301→+	t, err := parseTranscriptFile(sessionRef)
  1302→+	if err != nil {
  1303→+		if os.IsNotExist(err) {
  1304→+			return "", nil
  1305→+		}
  1306→+		return "", err
  1307→+	}
  1308→+
  1309→+	for i := len(t.Messages) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
  1310→+		msg := t.Messages[i]
  1311→+		if msg.Role == roleAssistant && msg.Content != "" {
  1312→+			return msg.Content, nil
  1313→+		}
  1314→+	}
  1315→+
  1316→+	return "", nil
  1317→+}
  1318→+
  1319→+// SliceFromMessage returns a JSON transcript containing only messages from startMessageIndex onward.
  1320→+// This is used by explain to scope a full transcript to a specific checkpoint's portion.
  1321→+func SliceFromMessage(data []byte, startMessageIndex int) []byte {
  1322→+	if len(data) == 0 || startMessageIndex <= 0 {
  1323→+		return data
  1324→+	}
  1325→+
  1326→+	t, err := ParseTranscript(data)
  1327→+	if err != nil {
  1328→+		return nil
  1329→+	}
  1330→+
  1331→+	if startMessageIndex >= len(t.Messages) {
  1332→+		return nil
  1333→+	}
  1334→+
  1335→+	scoped := &Transcript{
  1336→+		SessionID: t.SessionID,
  1337→+		Messages:  t.Messages[startMessageIndex:],
  1338→+	}
  1339→+
  1340→+	out, err := json.Marshal(scoped)
  1341→+	if err != nil {
  1342→+		return nil
  1343→+	}
  1344→+	return out
  1345→+}
  1346→+
  1347→+// ExtractAllUserPrompts extracts all user prompts from raw transcript bytes.
  1348→+// This is a package-level function used by the condensation path.
  1349→+func ExtractAllUserPrompts(data []byte) ([]string, error) {
  1350→+	t, err := ParseTranscript(data)
  1351→+	if err != nil {
  1352→+		return nil, err
  1353→+	}
  1354→+
  1355→+	var prompts []string
  1356→+	for _, msg := range t.Messages {
  1357→+		if msg.Role == roleUser && msg.Content != "" {
  1358→+			prompts = append(prompts, msg.Content)
  1359→+		}
  1360→+	}
  1361→+	return prompts, nil
  1362→+}
  1363→+
  1364→+// CalculateTokenUsageFromBytes computes token usage from raw transcript bytes starting at the given message offset.
  1365→+// This is a package-level function used by the condensation path (which has bytes, not a file path).
  1366→+func CalculateTokenUsageFromBytes(data []byte, startMessageIndex int) *agent.TokenUsage {
  1367→+	t, err := ParseTranscript(data)
  1368→+	if err != nil || t == nil {
  1369→+		return &agent.TokenUsage{}
  1370→+	}
  1371→+
  1372→+	usage := &agent.TokenUsage{}
  1373→+	for i := startMessageIndex; i < len(t.Messages); i++ {
  1374→+		msg := t.Messages[i]
  1375→+		if msg.Role != roleAssistant || msg.Tokens == nil {
  1376→+			continue
  1377→+		}
  1378→+		usage.InputTokens += msg.Tokens.Input
  1379→+		usage.OutputTokens += msg.Tokens.Output
  1380→+		usage.CacheReadTokens += msg.Tokens.Cache.Read
  1381→+		usage.CacheCreationTokens += msg.Tokens.Cache.Write
  1382→+		usage.APICallCount++
  1383→+	}
  1384→+
  1385→+	return usage
  1386→+}
  1387→+
  1388→+// CalculateTokenUsage computes token usage from assistant messages starting at the given offset.
  1389→+func (a *OpenCodeAgent) CalculateTokenUsage(sessionRef string, fromOffset int) (*agent.TokenUsage, error) {
  1390→+	t, err := parseTranscriptFile(sessionRef)
  1391→+	if err != nil {
  1392→+		if os.IsNotExist(err) {
  1393→+			return nil, nil //nolint:nilnil // nil usage for nonexistent file is expected
  1394→+		}
  1395→+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to parse transcript for token usage: %w", err)
  1396→+	}
  1397→+
  1398→+	usage := &agent.TokenUsage{}
  1399→+	for i := fromOffset; i < len(t.Messages); i++ {
  1400→+		msg := t.Messages[i]
  1401→+		if msg.Role != roleAssistant || msg.Tokens == nil {
  1402→+			continue
  1403→+		}
  1404→+		usage.InputTokens += msg.Tokens.Input
  1405→+		usage.OutputTokens += msg.Tokens.Output
  1406→+		usage.CacheReadTokens += msg.Tokens.Cache.Read
  1407→+		usage.CacheCreationTokens += msg.Tokens.Cache.Write
  1408→+		usage.APICallCount++
  1409→+	}
  1410→+
  1411→+	return usage, nil
  1412→+}

  1786→+func TestChunkTranscript_RoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
  1787→+	t.Parallel()
  1788→+	ag := &OpenCodeAgent{}
  1789→+	content := []byte(testTranscriptJSON)

  1791→+	// Split into chunks

  1793→+	if err != nil {

  1795→+	}
  1796→+
  1797→+	// Reassemble

  1799→+	if err != nil {
  1800→+		t.Fatalf("reassemble error: %v", err)
  1801→+	}
  1802→+
  1803→+	// Parse both and compare messages
  1804→+	original, parseErr := ParseTranscript(content)
  1805→+	if parseErr != nil {
  1806→+		t.Fatalf("failed to parse original: %v", parseErr)
  1807→+	}
  1808→+	result, parseErr := ParseTranscript(reassembled)
  1809→+	if parseErr != nil {
  1810→+		t.Fatalf("failed to parse reassembled: %v", parseErr)
  1811→+	}
  1812→+
  1813→+	if result.SessionID != original.SessionID {
  1814→+		t.Errorf("session_id mismatch: %q vs %q", result.SessionID, original.SessionID)
  1815→+	}
  1816→+	if len(result.Messages) != len(original.Messages) {
  1817→+		t.Fatalf("message count mismatch: %d vs %d", len(result.Messages), len(original.Messages))
  1818→+	}
  1819→+	for i, msg := range result.Messages {
  1820→+		if msg.ID != original.Messages[i].ID {
  1821→+			t.Errorf("message %d: ID mismatch %q vs %q", i, msg.ID, original.Messages[i].ID)
  1822→+		}
  1823→+	}
  1824→+}

# Event Type Definitions

	CreatedEvent EventType = "created"

## Complete File Content

```go
package pubsub

import "context"

const (
	CreatedEvent EventType = "created"
	UpdatedEvent EventType = "updated"
	DeletedEvent EventType = "deleted"
)

type Suscriber[T any] interface {
	Subscribe(context.Context) <-chan Event[T]
}

type (
	// EventType identifies the type of event
	EventType string

	// Event represents an event in the lifecycle of a resource
	Event[T any] struct {
		Type    EventType
		Payload T
	}

	Publisher[T any] interface {
		Publish(EventType, T)
	}
)
```

**Summary**: This Go package implements a generic publish-subscribe pattern with three lifecycle events (creation, modification, and deletion) that can be broadcast to subscribers through typed channels.

# Session Package Analysis

## Session Types

The primary domain type is `Session`, containing:
- Identity fields: `ID`, `ParentSessionID`
- Metadata: `Title`, `CreatedAt`, `UpdatedAt`
- Analytics: `MessageCount`, `PromptTokens`, `CompletionTokens`, `Cost`
- Content reference: `SummaryMessageID`

## Service Interface

The `Service` interface defines operations:
- **Creation**: `Create()`, `CreateTitleSession()`, `CreateTaskSession()`
- **Retrieval**: `Get()`, `List()`
- **Persistence**: `Save()`, `Delete()`
- **Events**: Inherits from `pubsub.Suscriber[Session]`

## Event Handling

The service publishes three event types via the pub/sub broker:
- `pubsub.CreatedEvent` - triggered after session creation
- `pubsub.UpdatedEvent` - triggered after session updates
- `pubsub.DeletedEvent` - triggered after session deletion

## Database Integration

The implementation uses a `db.Querier` abstraction with methods like `CreateSession()`, `UpdateSession()`, `DeleteSession()`, and `GetSessionByID()`. The `fromDBItem()` converter transforms database models to domain objects, handling nullable fields through `sql.NullString`.

## Architecture Pattern

This follows a domain-driven service pattern with pub/sub integration, separating business logic from database operations through the querier interface.

## Review: PR #415 — Add OpenCode agent support

### Summary

This PR adds OpenCode as a third supported coding agent (alongside Claude Code and Gemini CLI) across 18 files / ~2,169 lines. It includes an embedded TypeScript plugin, hook lifecycle handling, transcript parsing, condensation, explain scoping, and summarization support.

### Comparison with Other Open PRs

| | **#415 (this)** | **#341 (adrianmg)** | **#220 (ammarateya)** | **#315 (MementoMori123)** | **#257 (Avyukth)** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Files** | 18 | 22 | 11 | 6 | 19 |
| **Approach** | Embedded TS plugin → `entire hooks opencode` | Same plugin approach | Plugin approach + `opencode export` | No hooks (agent-managed) | Combined OpenCode + Codex + shared pipeline |
| **Transcript** | Plugin writes JSON from in-memory + SDK fallback | Plugin writes JSONL to tmpdir | Transcript reconstruction from `~/.local/share/opencode/storage/` | N/A (passthrough) | Git-status-based (no transcript parsing) |
| **Hooks** | 5 (session-start, session-end, turn-start, turn-end, compaction) | 4 (session-start, user-prompt-submit, stop, task) | 4 (prompt-submit, stop, session events) | 0 (SupportsHooks=false) | 3 (session-created, session-busy, session-idle) |
| **Tests** | Unit + summarize tests | 61 unit + 23 integration | Limited (transcript_test) | Registry test only | Unit tests for Codex + OpenCode |
| **Status** | Current branch | Maintainer asked to wait for #281 | Draft, told to wait for #281 | Told to wait for #281 | Told to wait for #281 |

**Key observation:** All open PRs have been told to wait for the agent interface refactor (#281). This PR seems to be from a maintainer (peyton-alt, on the same `feat/add-opencode` branch as PR #415), so it may be the "official" implementation.

### Correctness vs OpenCode Plugin Docs

**Events used vs available:**

The plugin docs list these session events: `session.created`, `session.compacted`, `session.deleted`, `session.diff`, `session.error`, `session.idle`, `session.status`, `session.updated`. Plus message events: `message.updated`, `message.part.updated`.

This PR uses:
- `session.created` — correct
- `message.updated` — correct (accumulates message metadata)
- `message.part.updated` — correct (accumulates parts per message)
- `session.idle` — correct (turn-end)
- `session.compacted` — correct
- `session.deleted` — correct (session-end)

Missing events that *could* be useful:
- `session.error` — not handled. If the session errors, no final transcript is written. Consider at least writing what's in memory.
- `session.diff` — not handled (reasonable, this is for UI diffing)
- `tool.execute.before` / `tool.execute.after` — not used, but could provide more accurate file-modification tracking

**Tool names (FileModificationTools):**

The PR defines: `edit_file`, `write`, `write_file`, `create_file`, `patch`

OpenCode's actual tool names from source: `edit`, `write`, `patch`

**Issue: `edit_file`, `write_file`, `create_file` don't exist in OpenCode.** The real tool names are `edit`, `write`, and `patch`. The current list appears to be borrowed from Claude Code's tool names. Since the plugin writes tool call data using OpenCode's part format, only the actual OpenCode tool names would appear. This means `edit` and `write` will match (they're in the list as `write`), but `edit_file` is wrong — the real tool is just `edit`. You'd miss edits.

**Transcript storage path:**

The plugin stores transcripts at `~/.opencode/sessions/entire/<sanitized-path>/<sessionId>.json`. This is a custom location (not OpenCode's native `~/.local/share/opencode/storage/`), which is fine since the plugin controls the writes. The Go side mirrors this with `SanitizePathForOpenCode()`. PR #220 took a different approach (reading from OpenCode's native storage), but this PR's approach is more reliable since it controls the format.

### Code Quality

**Strengths:**
1. Clean separation of concerns: `types.go`, `hooks.go`, `lifecycle.go`, `transcript.go`, `opencode.go`, `plugin.go`
2. Implements all relevant interfaces: `Agent`, `HookSupport`, `HookHandler`, `TranscriptAnalyzer`, `TokenCalculator`
3. Comprehensive tests for transcript parsing, chunking, reassembly, and lifecycle events
4. The plugin's dual-path transcript writing (SDK API with in-memory fallback for shutdown) is clever and robust
5. Condensation, explain, and summarize paths are all wired up
6. Proper `go:embed` for the plugin template
7. Good nolint annotations with explanations

**Issues:**

1. **FileModificationTools list is wrong** (as noted above). Should be `edit`, `write`, `patch` per OpenCode's source. Remove `edit_file`, `write_file`, `create_file`.

2. **`extractFilePathFromInput` key names may not match OpenCode's tool args.** OpenCode's `edit` tool takes `file_path` (confirmed via the docs plugin example), but `write` takes `file_path` too. The keys `file`, `filename` are speculative — verify against actual OpenCode tool arg schemas.

3. **Plugin `callHook` uses `echo ${json} | cmd`.** BunShell's `${}` interpolation is injection-safe (it quotes automatically), so this is OK. But the pattern of piping through echo means very large payloads could hit shell argument limits. Consider using `Bun.write` to a temp file + `< file` redirect for the turn-end hook (which includes the largest payloads).

4. **`session.deleted` cleanup clears ALL in-memory stores.** If OpenCode supports concurrent sessions (the docs mention multi-session capability), deleting one session would wipe the in-memory state for another. The stores should be keyed by session ID.

5. **`explain.go` has unreachable code.** After the `switch` block on lines 2011-2017, line 2018 still has `return transcript.SliceFromLine(...)`. The `case agent.AgentTypeClaudeCode, agent.AgentTypeUnknown:` + the default covers everything, making the trailing return dead code. Same issue in `transcriptOffset()`.

6. **`setup.go` `removeAgentHooks` is still hardcoded per-agent** rather than iterating the registry. PR #341 noted this and refactored it to use `agent.All()`. Consider doing the same to prevent this from growing with each agent.

7. **`FormatResumeCommand` returns `"opencode --session " + sessionID`** — verify this is the actual OpenCode CLI flag. The OpenCode repo doesn't seem to have a `--session` flag documented in its README.

8. **No integration tests.** PR #341 had 23 integration tests. This PR only has unit tests for the opencode package and summarize tests. The hook lifecycle (session-start → turn-start → turn-end → session-end with checkpoint creation/rewind) isn't integration-tested.

9. **`DetectPresence` falls back to `"."` when `RepoRoot()` fails** rather than propagating the error. This could give false positives if run outside a repo.

### Minor Observations

- The `extractGenericToolDetail` rename from `extractGeminiToolDetail` is a nice touch for reuse
- The `session.compacted` → "compaction" hook is forward-thinking (context window compaction is unique to OpenCode)
- `IsPreview() = true` is appropriate since OpenCode's plugin API may still change
- Tests properly handle `t.Parallel()` vs `t.Chdir()` per the CLAUDE.md guidelines

### Recommendations

1. **Fix `FileModificationTools`** to match OpenCode's actual tool names: `edit`, `write`, `patch`
2. **Add multi-session safety** to the plugin's in-memory stores (key by session ID)
3. **Handle `session.error`** in the plugin (write whatever's in memory before cleanup)
4. **Remove dead code** after the switch statements in `explain.go`
5. **Consider registry-based iteration** in `removeAgentHooks` instead of adding another hardcoded block
6. **Verify `--session` flag** for `FormatResumeCommand`
7. **Add integration tests** for the full hook lifecycle before merge

so ~/.opencode/sessions/entire/<sanitized-path>/<sessionId>.json is completely made up path?

> AGENT

Yes, completely invented. Let me trace it:

1. **OpenCode's actual storage** is SQLite at `~/.local/share/opencode/storage/` (XDG data dir). OpenCode doesn't write JSON/JSONL transcript files to disk at all.

2. **`~/.opencode/` at the home level doesn't exist as an OpenCode convention.** OpenCode uses:
   - `~/.config/opencode/` — global config
   - `~/.local/share/opencode/` — data (SQLite DB)
   - `~/.cache/opencode/` — cache (bun node_modules)
   - `.opencode/` **in the project directory** — project-level config and plugins

3. **This PR invents `~/.opencode/sessions/entire/`** as a home-level directory to dump transcripts that the TypeScript plugin reconstructs from in-memory message events.

The concern is that `~/.opencode/` *looks like* it belongs to OpenCode, but it doesn't. If OpenCode ever starts using `~/.opencode/` for its own purposes (not unlikely — many tools consolidate to `~/.<toolname>/`), this would silently conflict.

A more honest path would be something like:
- `~/.entire/opencode-sessions/<sanitized-path>/` — clearly Entire's directory
- `~/.local/share/entire/opencode-sessions/` — XDG-compliant
- Or even a temp directory (`os.TempDir()/entire-opencode/`) — which is what PR #341 used (`os.tmpdir()/entire-opencode/<sessionId>.jsonl`)

> AGENT

Right — Entire doesn't store anything outside the repo *of its own*. But it does **read** from outside the repo — specifically from each agent's *own* session directories:

| Agent | `GetSessionDir` path | Whose directory? |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | `~/.claude/projects/<sanitized>/` | Claude Code's own dir |
| Gemini CLI | `~/.gemini/tmp/<hash>/chats/` | Gemini CLI's own dir |
| **OpenCode** | `~/.opencode/sessions/entire/<sanitized>/` | **Invented by this PR** |

Claude Code and Gemini CLI both read transcripts from directories that **those agents themselves create and manage**. Entire just reads what's already there.

OpenCode is the odd one out — it doesn't write transcripts to disk at all (it uses SQLite). So this PR invents a new path *and* has the plugin write to it. The problem is it squats on `~/.opencode/` as if it belongs to OpenCode, when it's actually Entire creating and owning that data.

If the pattern is "read from the agent's own session directory," this breaks it. A more consistent approach would be to either:
- Store inside the repo (e.g., `.entire/opencode-sessions/`) to match Entire's "everything in the repo" pattern
- Or use a clearly Entire-owned path outside the repo if there's a good reason not to (e.g., `~/.entire/opencode-transcripts/`)

> AGENT

Now I have the full picture. Here's the data flow:

**For Claude Code / Gemini CLI:**
- The agent itself writes transcripts to its own home directory (`~/.claude/projects/...` / `~/.gemini/tmp/...`)
- Entire's hooks **read** from that agent-owned location via `event.SessionRef`
- On checkpoint save, the transcript bytes are copied into the shadow branch / `entire/checkpoints/v1`
- The `state.TranscriptPath` in `.git/entire-sessions/` just stores the path for mid-session reads

**For OpenCode (this PR):**
- OpenCode stores sessions in SQLite — no file-based transcripts exist
- So the plugin **invents a path** and writes reconstructed JSON there
- The Go handler reads from that same invented path

You're right — the transcript is really just a **handoff mechanism** between the TS plugin and the Go handler. Once it's saved to the shadow branch, the file on disk doesn't matter anymore.

To your question about `.git/entire-sessions/`: that currently only holds small session **state** JSON files (phase, base commit, checkpoint count, etc.), not full transcripts. But there's no reason it couldn't.

The real question is simpler than it seems:

**The plugin needs to write the transcript somewhere the Go handler can read it, within the same `turn-end` call.** After that, it gets copied to git refs and the file is disposable. So the options are:

1. **`os.TempDir()`** — most honest (it IS ephemeral). PR #341 did this.
2. **`.git/entire-sessions/transcripts/`** — keeps everything in the repo, under Entire's existing namespace. No squatting on `~/.opencode/`.
3. **`.entire/opencode/`** — in the repo working tree, already gitignored.

And no, you would NOT need to "feed data back into SQLite" for resume. OpenCode manages its own sessions via its own SQLite. `FormatResumeCommand("opencode --session <id>")` would tell OpenCode to resume from its own storage. Entire's transcript copy is for Entire's purposes only (checkpoint metadata, explain, summarize) — it's a one-way read.

> DEVELOPER

ok, then I agree we should go with os.TempDir()

> AGENT

I'll update both the TypeScript plugin and the Go side to use temp directories instead of the invented `~/.opencode/` path.

     1→// Entire CLI plugin for OpenCode
     2→// Auto-generated by `entire enable --agent opencode`
     3→// Do not edit manually — changes will be overwritten on next install.
     4→// Requires Bun runtime (used by OpenCode's plugin system for loading ESM plugins).
     5→import type { Plugin } from "@opencode-ai/plugin"
     6→
     7→export const EntirePlugin: Plugin = async ({ client, directory, $ }) => {
     8→  const ENTIRE_CMD = "__ENTIRE_CMD__"
     9→  // Store transcripts outside the repo (matches Go SanitizePathForOpenCode).
    10→  const home = Bun.env.HOME ?? ""
    11→  const sanitized = directory.replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9]/g, "-")
    12→  const transcriptDir = `${home}/.opencode/sessions/entire/${sanitized}`
    13→  const seenUserMessages = new Set<string>()
    14→
    15→  // In-memory stores — used to write transcripts without relying on the SDK API,
    16→  // which may be unavailable during shutdown.
    17→  // messageStore: keyed by message ID, stores message metadata (role, time, tokens, etc.)
    18→  const messageStore = new Map<string, any>()
    19→  // partStore: keyed by message ID, stores accumulated parts from message.part.updated events
    20→  const partStore = new Map<string, any[]>()
    21→  let currentSessionID: string | null = null
    22→
    23→  // Ensure transcript directory exists
    24→  await $`mkdir -p ${transcriptDir}`.quiet().nothrow()
    25→
    26→  /**
    27→   * Pipe JSON payload to an entire hooks command.
    28→   * Errors are logged but never thrown — plugin failures must not crash OpenCode.
    29→   */
    30→  async function callHook(hookName: string, payload: Record<string, unknown>) {
    31→    try {
    32→      const json = JSON.stringify(payload)
    33→      await $`echo ${json} | ${ENTIRE_CMD} hooks opencode ${hookName}`.quiet().nothrow()
    34→    } catch {
    35→      // Silently ignore — plugin failures must not crash OpenCode
    36→    }
    37→  }
    38→
    39→  /** Extract text content from a list of parts. */
    40→  function textFromParts(parts: any[]): string {
    41→    return parts
    42→      .filter((p: any) => p.type === "text")
    43→      .map((p: any) => p.text ?? "")
    44→      .join("\n")
    45→  }
    46→
    47→  /** Format a message for the transcript using its accumulated parts. */
    48→  function formatMessageFromStore(msg: any) {
    49→    const parts = partStore.get(msg.id) ?? []
    50→    return {
    51→      id: msg.id,
    52→      role: msg.role,
    53→      content: textFromParts(parts),
    54→      time: msg.time,
    55→      ...(msg.role === "assistant" ? {
    56→        tokens: msg.tokens,
    57→        cost: msg.cost,
    58→        parts: parts.map((p: any) => ({
    59→          type: p.type,
    60→          ...(p.type === "text" ? { text: p.text } : {}),
    61→          ...(p.type === "tool" ? { tool: p.tool, callID: p.callID, state: p.state } : {}),
    62→        })),
    63→      } : {}),
    64→    }
    65→  }
    66→
    67→  /** Format a message from an API response (which includes parts inline). */
    68→  function formatMessageFromAPI(info: any, parts: any[]) {
    69→    return {
    70→      id: info.id,
    71→      role: info.role,
    72→      content: textFromParts(parts),
    73→      time: info.time,
    74→      ...(info.role === "assistant" ? {
    75→        tokens: info.tokens,
    76→        cost: info.cost,
    77→        parts: parts.map((p: any) => ({
    78→          type: p.type,
    79→          ...(p.type === "text" ? { text: p.text } : {}),
    80→          ...(p.type === "tool" ? { tool: p.tool, callID: p.callID, state: p.state } : {}),
    81→        })),
    82→      } : {}),
    83→    }
    84→  }
    85→
    86→  /**
    87→   * Write transcript from in-memory stores (messageStore + partStore).
    88→   * This does NOT call the SDK API, so it works even during shutdown.
    89→   */
    90→  async function writeTranscriptFromMemory(sessionID: string): Promise<string> {
    91→    const transcriptPath = `${transcriptDir}/${sessionID}.json`
    92→    try {
    93→      const messages = Array.from(messageStore.values())
    94→        .sort((a, b) => (a.time?.created ?? 0) - (b.time?.created ?? 0))
    95→
    96→      const transcript = {
    97→        session_id: sessionID,
    98→        messages: messages.map(formatMessageFromStore),
    99→      }
   100→      await Bun.write(transcriptPath, JSON.stringify(transcript))
   101→    } catch {
   102→      // Silently ignore write failures
   103→    }
   104→    return transcriptPath
   105→  }
   106→
   107→  /**
   108→   * Try to fetch messages via the SDK API (returns messages with parts inline)
   109→   * and write transcript. Falls back to in-memory stores if the API is unavailable.
   110→   */
   111→  async function writeTranscriptWithFallback(sessionID: string): Promise<string> {
   112→    const transcriptPath = `${transcriptDir}/${sessionID}.json`
   113→    try {
   114→      const response = await client.session.message.list({ path: { id: sessionID } })
   115→      // API returns Array<{ info: Message, parts: Array<Part> }>
   116→      const items = response.data ?? []
   117→
   118→      const transcript = {
   119→        session_id: sessionID,
   120→        messages: items.map((item: any) => formatMessageFromAPI(item.info, item.parts ?? [])),
   121→      }
   122→      await Bun.write(transcriptPath, JSON.stringify(transcript))
   123→      return transcriptPath
   124→    } catch {
   125→      // API unavailable (likely shutting down) — fall back to in-memory stores
   126→      return writeTranscriptFromMemory(sessionID)
   127→    }
   128→  }
   129→
   130→  return {
   131→    event: async ({ event }) => {
   132→      switch (event.type) {
   133→        case "session.created": {
   134→          const session = (event as any).properties?.info
   135→          if (!session?.id) break
   136→          currentSessionID = session.id
   137→          await callHook("session-start", {
   138→            session_id: session.id,
   139→            transcript_path: `${transcriptDir}/${session.id}.json`,
   140→          })
   141→          break
   142→        }
   143→
   144→        case "message.updated": {
   145→          const msg = (event as any).properties?.info
   146→          if (!msg) break
   147→          // Store message metadata (role, time, tokens, etc.)
   148→          // Content is NOT on the message — it arrives via message.part.updated events.
   149→          messageStore.set(msg.id, msg)
   150→          break
   151→        }
   152→
   153→        case "message.part.updated": {
   154→          const part = (event as any).properties?.part
   155→          if (!part?.messageID) break
   156→
   157→          // Accumulate parts per message
   158→          const existing = partStore.get(part.messageID) ?? []
   159→          // Replace existing part with same id, or append new one
   160→          const idx = existing.findIndex((p: any) => p.id === part.id)
   161→          if (idx >= 0) {
   162→            existing[idx] = part
   163→          } else {
   164→            existing.push(part)
   165→          }
   166→          partStore.set(part.messageID, existing)
   167→
   168→          // Fire turn-start on the first text part of a new user message
   169→          const msg = messageStore.get(part.messageID)
   170→          if (msg?.role === "user" && part.type === "text" && !seenUserMessages.has(msg.id)) {
   171→            seenUserMessages.add(msg.id)
   172→            const sessionID = msg.sessionID ?? currentSessionID
   173→            if (sessionID) {
   174→              await callHook("turn-start", {
   175→                session_id: sessionID,
   176→                transcript_path: `${transcriptDir}/${sessionID}.json`,
   177→                prompt: part.text ?? "",
   178→              })
   179→            }
   180→          }
   181→          break
   182→        }
   183→
   184→        case "session.idle": {
   185→          const sessionID = (event as any).properties?.sessionID
   186→          if (!sessionID) break
   187→          const transcriptPath = await writeTranscriptWithFallback(sessionID)
   188→          await callHook("turn-end", {
   189→            session_id: sessionID,
   190→            transcript_path: transcriptPath,
   191→          })
   192→          break
   193→        }
   194→
   195→        case "session.compacted": {
   196→          const sessionID = (event as any).properties?.sessionID
   197→          if (!sessionID) break
   198→          await callHook("compaction", {
   199→            session_id: sessionID,
   200→            transcript_path: `${transcriptDir}/${sessionID}.json`,
   201→          })
   202→          break
   203→        }
   204→
   205→        case "session.deleted": {
   206→          const session = (event as any).properties?.info
   207→          if (!session?.id) break
   208→          // Write final transcript before signaling session end
   209→          if (messageStore.size > 0) {
   210→            await writeTranscriptFromMemory(session.id)
   211→          }
   212→          seenUserMessages.clear()
   213→          messageStore.clear()
   214→          partStore.clear()
   215→          currentSessionID = null
   216→          await callHook("session-end", {
   217→            session_id: session.id,
   218→            transcript_path: `${transcriptDir}/${session.id}.json`,
   219→          })
   220→          break
   221→        }
   222→      }
   223→    },
   224→  }
   225→}

    63→func (a *OpenCodeAgent) ChunkTranscript(content []byte, maxSize int) ([][]byte, error) {
    64→	// OpenCode uses JSON format (like Gemini). Parse and split by messages.
    65→	if len(content) <= maxSize {
    66→		return [][]byte{content}, nil
    67→	}
    68→
    69→	var transcript Transcript
    70→	if err := json.Unmarshal(content, &transcript); err != nil {
    71→		// Fallback to JSONL chunking if not valid JSON
    72→		chunks, chunkErr := agent.ChunkJSONL(content, maxSize)
    73→		if chunkErr != nil {
    74→			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to chunk transcript as JSONL: %w", chunkErr)
    75→		}
    76→		return chunks, nil
    77→	}
    78→
    79→	if len(transcript.Messages) == 0 {
    80→		return [][]byte{content}, nil
    81→	}
    82→
    83→	// Pre-marshal each message to avoid O(n²) re-serialization.
    84→	// Track running size and split at chunk boundaries (same approach as Gemini).
    85→	var chunks [][]byte
    86→	var currentMessages []Message
    87→	baseSize := len(fmt.Sprintf(`{"session_id":%q,"messages":[]}`, transcript.SessionID))
    88→	currentSize := baseSize
    89→
    90→	for _, msg := range transcript.Messages {
    91→		msgBytes, err := json.Marshal(msg)
    92→		if err != nil {
    93→			continue // Skip messages that fail to marshal
    94→		}
    95→		msgSize := len(msgBytes) + 1 // +1 for comma separator
    96→
    97→		if currentSize+msgSize > maxSize && len(currentMessages) > 0 {
    98→			// Save current chunk
    99→			chunkData, marshalErr := json.Marshal(Transcript{
   100→				SessionID: transcript.SessionID,
   101→				Messages:  currentMessages,
   102→			})
   103→			if marshalErr != nil {
   104→				return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal transcript chunk: %w", marshalErr)
   105→			}
   106→			chunks = append(chunks, chunkData)
   107→
   108→			// Start new chunk
   109→			currentMessages = nil
   110→			currentSize = baseSize
   111→		}
   112→
   113→		currentMessages = append(currentMessages, msg)
   114→		currentSize += msgSize
   115→	}
   116→
   117→	// Save remaining messages
   118→	if len(currentMessages) > 0 {
   119→		chunkData, err := json.Marshal(Transcript{
   120→			SessionID: transcript.SessionID,
   121→			Messages:  currentMessages,
   122→		})
   123→		if err != nil {
   124→			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal final transcript chunk: %w", err)
   125→		}
   126→		chunks = append(chunks, chunkData)
   127→	}
   128→
   129→	return chunks, nil
   130→}
   131→
   132→func (a *OpenCodeAgent) ReassembleTranscript(chunks [][]byte) ([]byte, error) {
   133→	if len(chunks) == 0 {
   134→		return nil, nil
   135→	}
   136→	if len(chunks) == 1 {
   137→		return chunks[0], nil
   138→	}
   139→
   140→	var combined Transcript
   141→	for i, chunk := range chunks {
   142→		var t Transcript
   143→		if err := json.Unmarshal(chunk, &t); err != nil {
   144→			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to parse transcript chunk %d: %w", i, err)
   145→		}
   146→		if i == 0 {
   147→			combined.SessionID = t.SessionID
   148→		}
   149→		combined.Messages = append(combined.Messages, t.Messages...)
   150→	}

   152→	data, err := json.Marshal(combined)
   153→	if err != nil {
   154→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal reassembled transcript: %w", err)
   155→	}
   156→	return data, nil
   157→}

   226→func (a *OpenCodeAgent) WriteSession(session *agent.AgentSession) error {

**`types.go`**: Replaced `["edit_file", "write", "write_file", "create_file", "patch"]` with `["edit", "write", "patch"]` — the actual tool names from OpenCode's source (`EditToolName`, `WriteToolName`, `PatchToolName`).

> DEVELOPER

but wondering now: so basically we condens this into an OpenCode like script?

> AGENT

Good question — let me trace the full lifecycle of this transcript data:

1. **Plugin** accumulates messages in memory from OpenCode events → writes a JSON file to `/tmp/entire-opencode/...`
2. **Hook handler** reads that JSON file → passes it to `SaveStep` as the transcript
3. **Shadow branch** stores it verbatim as `full.jsonl` (despite being JSON, not JSONL — that filename is a holdover from Claude Code)
4. **Condensation** (on user commit) copies it to `entire/checkpoints/v1` — still the same JSON blob
5. **Explain/summarize** parse it later using the OpenCode-specific parsers

So yes — the plugin is essentially reconstructing an "OpenCode-like" transcript from event streams, writing it as JSON, and then the whole Entire pipeline treats it as the canonical transcript for that session.

The question is whether all this reconstruction is worth it, or if there's a simpler approach. The plugin could just send the essentials in the hook payloads themselves:
- `turn-start`: already sends `prompt`
- `turn-end`: could send `modified_files`, `token_usage` directly — the plugin has access to the SDK client

That would eliminate the transcript file entirely. The hook handler would get everything it needs from stdin. The downside is you'd lose `explain` and `summarize` support (which need the full conversation to work). But those are arguably lower priority for a preview agent.

What's your preference — keep the full transcript reconstruction for feature parity, or simplify to payload-only for now?

> DEVELOPER

yeah we want some kind of log, and I feel generating it Claude Code like is a good idea for now. But if it's JSON it's not identical to Claude Code so maybe we should fix that?

> AGENT

Yeah, converting to JSONL would be a good simplification. Right now every downstream consumer needs OpenCode-specific branches just for **format handling** (JSON blob vs JSONL lines), even though the actual content parsing is the same concept.

If the plugin writes JSONL (one message per line), then:

- `explain.go`: both `scopeTranscriptForCheckpoint` and `transcriptOffset` can drop the OpenCode cases — line-based slicing just works
- `manual_commit_condensation.go`: `countTranscriptItems` can count lines instead of parsing JSON
- `ChunkTranscript` / `ReassembleTranscript`: can use the existing `agent.ChunkJSONL` helper instead of custom JSON splitting
- `full.jsonl` actually IS JSONL

The message **schema** stays OpenCode-native (role, parts, tokens, etc.) — only the **container format** changes from a JSON array to one-object-per-line. The content-level parsers (`ExtractModifiedFiles`, `ExtractPrompts`, `CalculateTokenUsage`) still need to understand OpenCode's message shape, but that's fine.

Want me to make this change? The scope would be:
1. **Plugin**: write one message per line instead of `{"session_id":..., "messages":[...]}`
2. **Go transcript.go**: rewrite parsers to read JSONL lines
3. **Go explain.go / condensation**: remove the OpenCode-specific format branches
4. **Tests**: update fixtures from JSON to JSONL

> DEVELOPER

yes
