   909→// GitCommitWithShadowHooks stages and commits files, simulating the prepare-commit-msg
   910→// and post-commit hooks as a human (with TTY). This is the default for tests.
   911→func (env *TestEnv) GitCommitWithShadowHooks(message string, files ...string) {
   912→	env.T.Helper()
   913→	env.gitCommitWithShadowHooks(message, true, files...)
   914→}
   915→
   916→// GitCommitWithShadowHooksAsAgent is like GitCommitWithShadowHooks but simulates
   917→// an agent commit (no TTY). This triggers the fast path in PrepareCommitMsg that
   918→// skips content detection and interactive prompts for ACTIVE sessions.
   919→func (env *TestEnv) GitCommitWithShadowHooksAsAgent(message string, files ...string) {
   920→	env.T.Helper()
   921→	env.gitCommitWithShadowHooks(message, false, files...)
   922→}
   923→
   924→// gitCommitWithShadowHooks is the shared implementation for committing with shadow hooks.
   925→// When simulateTTY is true, sets ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=1 to simulate a human at the terminal.
   926→// When false, filters it out to simulate an agent subprocess (no controlling terminal).
   927→func (env *TestEnv) gitCommitWithShadowHooks(message string, simulateTTY bool, files ...string) {
   928→	env.T.Helper()
   929→
   930→	// Stage files using go-git
   931→	for _, file := range files {
   932→		env.GitAdd(file)
   933→	}
   934→
   935→	// Create a temp file for the commit message (prepare-commit-msg hook modifies this)
   936→	msgFile := filepath.Join(env.RepoDir, ".git", "COMMIT_EDITMSG")
   937→	if err := os.WriteFile(msgFile, []byte(message), 0o644); err != nil {
   938→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to write commit message file: %v", err)
   939→	}
   940→
   941→	// Run prepare-commit-msg hook using the shared binary.
   942→	// Pass source="message" to match real `git commit -m` behavior.
   943→	prepCmd := exec.Command(getTestBinary(), "hooks", "git", "prepare-commit-msg", msgFile, "message")
   944→	prepCmd.Dir = env.RepoDir
   945→	if simulateTTY {
   946→		// Simulate human at terminal: ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=1 makes hasTTY() return true
   947→		// and askConfirmTTY() return defaultYes without reading from /dev/tty.
   948→		prepCmd.Env = append(os.Environ(), "ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=1")
   949→	} else {
   950→		// Simulate agent: ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=0 makes hasTTY() return false,
   951→		// triggering the fast path that adds trailers for ACTIVE sessions.
   952→		prepCmd.Env = append(os.Environ(), "ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=0")
   953→	}
   954→	if output, err := prepCmd.CombinedOutput(); err != nil {
   955→		env.T.Logf("prepare-commit-msg output: %s", output)
   956→		// Don't fail - hook may silently succeed
   957→	}
   958→
   959→	// Read the modified message
   960→	modifiedMsg, err := os.ReadFile(msgFile)
   961→	if err != nil {
   962→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to read modified commit message: %v", err)
   963→	}
   964→
   965→	// Create the commit using go-git with the modified message
   966→	repo, err := git.PlainOpen(env.RepoDir)
   967→	if err != nil {
   968→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to open git repo: %v", err)
   969→	}
   970→
   971→	worktree, err := repo.Worktree()
   972→	if err != nil {
   973→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to get worktree: %v", err)
   974→	}
   975→
   976→	_, err = worktree.Commit(string(modifiedMsg), &git.CommitOptions{
   977→		Author: &object.Signature{
   978→			Name:  "Test User",
   979→			Email: "test@example.com",
   980→			When:  time.Now(),
   981→		},
   982→	})
   983→	if err != nil {
   984→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to commit: %v", err)
   985→	}
   986→
   987→	// Run post-commit hook using the shared binary
   988→	// This triggers condensation if the commit has an Entire-Checkpoint trailer
   989→	postCmd := exec.Command(getTestBinary(), "hooks", "git", "post-commit")
   990→	postCmd.Dir = env.RepoDir
   991→	if output, err := postCmd.CombinedOutput(); err != nil {
   992→		env.T.Logf("post-commit output: %s", output)
   993→		// Don't fail - hook may silently succeed
   994→	}
   995→}
   996→
   997→// GitCommitAmendWithShadowHooks amends the last commit with shadow hooks.
   998→// This simulates `git commit --amend` with the prepare-commit-msg and post-commit hooks.
   999→// The prepare-commit-msg hook is called with "commit" source to indicate an amend.
  1000→func (env *TestEnv) GitCommitAmendWithShadowHooks(message string, files ...string) {
  1001→	env.T.Helper()
  1002→
  1003→	// Stage any additional files
  1004→	for _, file := range files {
  1005→		env.GitAdd(file)
  1006→	}
  1007→
  1008→	// Write commit message to temp file
  1009→	msgFile := filepath.Join(env.RepoDir, ".git", "COMMIT_EDITMSG")
  1010→	if err := os.WriteFile(msgFile, []byte(message), 0o644); err != nil {
  1011→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to write commit message file: %v", err)
  1012→	}
  1013→
  1014→	// Run prepare-commit-msg hook with "commit" source (indicates amend).
  1015→	// Set ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=1 to simulate human (amend is always a human operation).
  1016→	prepCmd := exec.Command(getTestBinary(), "hooks", "git", "prepare-commit-msg", msgFile, "commit")
  1017→	prepCmd.Dir = env.RepoDir
  1018→	prepCmd.Env = append(os.Environ(), "ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=1")
  1019→	if output, err := prepCmd.CombinedOutput(); err != nil {
  1020→		env.T.Logf("prepare-commit-msg (amend) output: %s", output)
  1021→	}
  1022→
  1023→	// Read the modified message
  1024→	modifiedMsg, err := os.ReadFile(msgFile)
  1025→	if err != nil {
  1026→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to read modified commit message: %v", err)
  1027→	}
  1028→
  1029→	// Amend the commit using go-git
  1030→	repo, err := git.PlainOpen(env.RepoDir)
  1031→	if err != nil {
  1032→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to open git repo: %v", err)
  1033→	}
  1034→
  1035→	worktree, err := repo.Worktree()
  1036→	if err != nil {
  1037→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to get worktree: %v", err)
  1038→	}
  1039→
  1040→	_, err = worktree.Commit(string(modifiedMsg), &git.CommitOptions{
  1041→		Author: &object.Signature{
  1042→			Name:  "Test User",
  1043→			Email: "test@example.com",
  1044→			When:  time.Now(),
  1045→		},
  1046→		Amend: true,
  1047→	})
  1048→	if err != nil {
  1049→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to amend commit: %v", err)
  1050→	}
  1051→
  1052→	// Run post-commit hook
  1053→	postCmd := exec.Command(getTestBinary(), "hooks", "git", "post-commit")
  1054→	postCmd.Dir = env.RepoDir
  1055→	if output, err := postCmd.CombinedOutput(); err != nil {
  1056→		env.T.Logf("post-commit (amend) output: %s", output)
  1057→	}

  1060→// GitCommitWithTrailerRemoved stages and commits files, simulating what happens when
  1061→// a user removes the Entire-Checkpoint trailer during commit message editing.
  1062→// This tests the opt-out behavior where removing the trailer skips condensation.
  1063→func (env *TestEnv) GitCommitWithTrailerRemoved(message string, files ...string) {
  1064→	env.T.Helper()
  1065→
  1066→	// Stage files using go-git
  1067→	for _, file := range files {
  1068→		env.GitAdd(file)
  1069→	}
  1070→
  1071→	// Create a temp file for the commit message (prepare-commit-msg hook modifies this)
  1072→	msgFile := filepath.Join(env.RepoDir, ".git", "COMMIT_EDITMSG")
  1073→	if err := os.WriteFile(msgFile, []byte(message), 0o644); err != nil {
  1074→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to write commit message file: %v", err)
  1075→	}
  1076→
  1077→	// Run prepare-commit-msg hook using the shared binary.
  1078→	// Set ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=1 to simulate human (this tests the editor flow where
  1079→	// the user removes the trailer before committing).
  1080→	prepCmd := exec.Command(getTestBinary(), "hooks", "git", "prepare-commit-msg", msgFile)
  1081→	prepCmd.Dir = env.RepoDir
  1082→	prepCmd.Env = append(os.Environ(), "ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=1")
  1083→	if output, err := prepCmd.CombinedOutput(); err != nil {
  1084→		env.T.Logf("prepare-commit-msg output: %s", output)
  1085→	}
  1086→
  1087→	// Read the modified message (with trailer added by hook)
  1088→	modifiedMsg, err := os.ReadFile(msgFile)
  1089→	if err != nil {
  1090→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to read modified commit message: %v", err)
  1091→	}
  1092→
  1093→	// REMOVE the Entire-Checkpoint trailer (simulating user editing the message)
  1094→	lines := strings.Split(string(modifiedMsg), "\n")
  1095→	var cleanedLines []string
  1096→	for _, line := range lines {
  1097→		// Skip the trailer and the comments about it
  1098→		if strings.HasPrefix(line, "Entire-Checkpoint:") {
  1099→			continue
  1100→		}
  1101→		if strings.Contains(line, "Remove the Entire-Checkpoint trailer") {
  1102→			continue
  1103→		}
  1104→		if strings.Contains(line, "trailer will be added to your next commit") {
  1105→			continue
  1106→		}
  1107→		cleanedLines = append(cleanedLines, line)
  1108→	}
  1109→	cleanedMsg := strings.TrimRight(strings.Join(cleanedLines, "\n"), "\n") + "\n"
  1110→
  1111→	// Create the commit using go-git with the cleaned message (no trailer)
  1112→	repo, err := git.PlainOpen(env.RepoDir)
  1113→	if err != nil {
  1114→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to open git repo: %v", err)
  1115→	}
  1116→
  1117→	worktree, err := repo.Worktree()
  1118→	if err != nil {
  1119→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to get worktree: %v", err)
  1120→	}
  1121→
  1122→	_, err = worktree.Commit(cleanedMsg, &git.CommitOptions{
  1123→		Author: &object.Signature{
  1124→			Name:  "Test User",
  1125→			Email: "test@example.com",
  1126→			When:  time.Now(),
  1127→		},
  1128→	})
  1129→	if err != nil {
  1130→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to commit: %v", err)
  1131→	}
  1132→
  1133→	// Run post-commit hook - since trailer was removed, no condensation should happen
  1134→	postCmd := exec.Command(getTestBinary(), "hooks", "git", "post-commit")
  1135→	postCmd.Dir = env.RepoDir
  1136→	if output, err := postCmd.CombinedOutput(); err != nil {
  1137→		env.T.Logf("post-commit output: %s", output)
  1138→	}
  1139→}

  1219→// ListBranchesWithPrefix returns all branches that start with the given prefix.
  1220→func (env *TestEnv) ListBranchesWithPrefix(prefix string) []string {
  1221→	env.T.Helper()
  1222→
  1223→	repo, err := git.PlainOpen(env.RepoDir)
  1224→	if err != nil {
  1225→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to open git repo: %v", err)
  1226→	}
  1227→
  1228→	refs, err := repo.References()
  1229→	if err != nil {
  1230→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to get references: %v", err)
  1231→	}
  1232→
  1233→	var branches []string
  1234→	_ = refs.ForEach(func(ref *plumbing.Reference) error {
  1235→		name := ref.Name().Short()
  1236→		if len(name) >= len(prefix) && name[:len(prefix)] == prefix {
  1237→			branches = append(branches, name)
  1238→		}
  1239→		return nil
  1240→	})
  1241→
  1242→	return branches
  1243→}

  1245→// GetLatestCheckpointID returns the most recent checkpoint ID from the entire/checkpoints/v1 branch.
  1246→// This is used by tests that previously extracted the checkpoint ID from commit message trailers.
  1247→// Now that active branch commits are clean (no trailers), we get the ID from the sessions branch.
  1248→// Fatals if the checkpoint ID cannot be found, with detailed context about what was found.
  1249→func (env *TestEnv) GetLatestCheckpointID() string {
  1250→	env.T.Helper()
  1251→
  1252→	repo, err := git.PlainOpen(env.RepoDir)
  1253→	if err != nil {
  1254→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to open git repo: %v", err)
  1255→	}
  1256→
  1257→	// Get the entire/checkpoints/v1 branch
  1258→	refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(paths.MetadataBranchName)
  1259→	ref, err := repo.Reference(refName, true)
  1260→	if err != nil {
  1261→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to get %s branch: %v", paths.MetadataBranchName, err)
  1262→	}
  1263→
  1264→	commit, err := repo.CommitObject(ref.Hash())
  1265→	if err != nil {
  1266→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to get commit: %v", err)
  1267→	}
  1268→
  1269→	// Extract checkpoint ID from commit message
  1270→	// Format: "Checkpoint: <12-hex-char-id>\n\nSession: ...\nStrategy: ..."
  1271→	for _, line := range strings.Split(commit.Message, "\n") {
  1272→		line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
  1273→		if strings.HasPrefix(line, "Checkpoint: ") {
  1274→			return strings.TrimPrefix(line, "Checkpoint: ")
  1275→		}
  1276→	}
  1277→
  1278→	env.T.Fatalf("could not find checkpoint ID in %s branch commit message:\n%s",
  1279→		paths.MetadataBranchName, commit.Message)
  1280→	return ""
  1281→}

  1286→func (env *TestEnv) TryGetLatestCheckpointID() string {
  1287→	env.T.Helper()

  1292→	}

  1296→	ref, err := repo.Reference(refName, true)
  1297→	if err != nil {
  1298→		return ""
  1299→	}
  1300→
  1301→	commit, err := repo.CommitObject(ref.Hash())
  1302→	if err != nil {

  1304→	}

  1308→	for _, line := range strings.Split(commit.Message, "\n") {

  1323→// GetCheckpointIDFromCommitMessage extracts the Entire-Checkpoint trailer from a commit message.
  1324→// Returns empty string if no trailer found.
  1325→func (env *TestEnv) GetCheckpointIDFromCommitMessage(commitSHA string) string {
  1326→	env.T.Helper()
  1327→
  1328→	msg := env.GetCommitMessage(commitSHA)
  1329→	cpID, found := trailers.ParseCheckpoint(msg)
  1330→	if !found {
  1331→		return ""
  1332→	}
  1333→	return cpID.String()
  1334→}
  1335→
  1336→// GetLatestCheckpointIDFromHistory walks backwards from HEAD on the active branch
  1337→// and returns the checkpoint ID from the first commit that has an Entire-Checkpoint trailer.
  1338→// This verifies that condensation actually happened (commit has trailer) without relying
  1339→// on timestamp-based matching.
  1340→func (env *TestEnv) GetLatestCheckpointIDFromHistory() string {
  1341→	env.T.Helper()
  1342→
  1343→	repo, err := git.PlainOpen(env.RepoDir)
  1344→	if err != nil {
  1345→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to open git repo: %v", err)
  1346→	}
  1347→
  1348→	head, err := repo.Head()
  1349→	if err != nil {
  1350→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to get HEAD: %v", err)
  1351→	}
  1352→
  1353→	commitIter, err := repo.Log(&git.LogOptions{From: head.Hash()})
  1354→	if err != nil {
  1355→		env.T.Fatalf("failed to iterate commits: %v", err)
  1356→	}
  1357→
  1358→	var checkpointID string
  1359→	//nolint:errcheck // ForEach callback handles errors
  1360→	commitIter.ForEach(func(c *object.Commit) error {
  1361→		if cpID, found := trailers.ParseCheckpoint(c.Message); found {
  1362→			checkpointID = cpID.String()
  1363→			return errors.New("stop iteration") // Found it, stop
  1364→		}
  1365→		return nil
  1366→	})
  1367→
  1368→	if checkpointID == "" {
  1369→		env.T.Fatalf("no commit with Entire-Checkpoint trailer found in history")
  1370→	}
  1371→
  1372→	return checkpointID
  1373→}

  1399→// CheckpointValidation contains expected values for checkpoint validation.
  1400→type CheckpointValidation struct {
  1401→	// CheckpointID is the expected checkpoint ID
  1402→	CheckpointID string
  1403→
  1404→	// SessionID is the expected session ID
  1405→	SessionID string
  1406→
  1407→	// Strategy is the expected strategy name
  1408→	Strategy string
  1409→
  1410→	// FilesTouched are the expected files in files_touched
  1411→	FilesTouched []string
  1412→
  1413→	// ExpectedPrompts are strings that should appear in prompt.txt
  1414→	ExpectedPrompts []string
  1415→
  1416→	// ExpectedTranscriptContent are strings that should appear in full.jsonl
  1417→	ExpectedTranscriptContent []string
  1418→
  1419→	// CheckpointsCount is the expected checkpoint count (0 means don't validate)
  1420→	CheckpointsCount int
  1421→}
  1422→
  1423→// ValidateCheckpoint performs comprehensive validation of a checkpoint on the metadata branch.
  1424→// It validates:
  1425→// - Root metadata.json (CheckpointSummary) structure and expected fields
  1426→// - Session metadata.json (CommittedMetadata) structure and expected fields
  1427→// - Transcript file (full.jsonl) is valid JSONL and contains expected content
  1428→// - Content hash file (content_hash.txt) matches SHA256 of transcript
  1429→// - Prompt file (prompt.txt) contains expected prompts
  1430→func (env *TestEnv) ValidateCheckpoint(v CheckpointValidation) {
  1431→	env.T.Helper()
  1432→
  1433→	// Validate root metadata.json (CheckpointSummary)
  1434→	env.validateCheckpointSummary(v)
  1435→
  1436→	// Validate session metadata.json (CommittedMetadata)
  1437→	env.validateSessionMetadata(v)
  1438→
  1439→	// Validate transcript is valid JSONL
  1440→	env.validateTranscriptJSONL(v.CheckpointID, v.ExpectedTranscriptContent)
  1441→
  1442→	// Validate content hash matches transcript
  1443→	env.validateContentHash(v.CheckpointID)
  1444→
  1445→	// Validate prompt.txt contains expected prompts
  1446→	if len(v.ExpectedPrompts) > 0 {
  1447→		env.validatePromptContent(v.CheckpointID, v.ExpectedPrompts)
  1448→	}
  1449→}
  1450→
  1451→// validateCheckpointSummary validates the root metadata.json (CheckpointSummary).
  1452→func (env *TestEnv) validateCheckpointSummary(v CheckpointValidation) {
  1453→	env.T.Helper()
  1454→
  1455→	summaryPath := CheckpointSummaryPath(v.CheckpointID)
  1456→	content, found := env.ReadFileFromBranch(paths.MetadataBranchName, summaryPath)
  1457→	if !found {
  1458→		env.T.Fatalf("CheckpointSummary not found at %s", summaryPath)
  1459→	}
  1460→
  1461→	var summary checkpoint.CheckpointSummary
  1462→	if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(content), &summary); err != nil {
  1463→		env.T.Fatalf("Failed to parse CheckpointSummary: %v\nContent: %s", err, content)
  1464→	}
  1465→
  1466→	// Validate checkpoint_id
  1467→	if summary.CheckpointID.String() != v.CheckpointID {
  1468→		env.T.Errorf("CheckpointSummary.CheckpointID = %q, want %q", summary.CheckpointID, v.CheckpointID)
  1469→	}
  1470→
  1471→	// Validate strategy
  1472→	if v.Strategy != "" && summary.Strategy != v.Strategy {
  1473→		env.T.Errorf("CheckpointSummary.Strategy = %q, want %q", summary.Strategy, v.Strategy)
  1474→	}
  1475→
  1476→	// Validate sessions array is populated
  1477→	if len(summary.Sessions) == 0 {
  1478→		env.T.Error("CheckpointSummary.Sessions should have at least one entry")
  1479→	}
  1480→
  1481→	// Validate files_touched
  1482→	if len(v.FilesTouched) > 0 {
  1483→		touchedSet := make(map[string]bool)
  1484→		for _, f := range summary.FilesTouched {
  1485→			touchedSet[f] = true
  1486→		}
  1487→		for _, expected := range v.FilesTouched {
  1488→			if !touchedSet[expected] {
  1489→				env.T.Errorf("CheckpointSummary.FilesTouched missing %q, got %v", expected, summary.FilesTouched)
  1490→			}
  1491→		}
  1492→	}
  1493→
  1494→	// Validate checkpoints_count
  1495→	if v.CheckpointsCount > 0 && summary.CheckpointsCount != v.CheckpointsCount {
  1496→		env.T.Errorf("CheckpointSummary.CheckpointsCount = %d, want %d", summary.CheckpointsCount, v.CheckpointsCount)
  1497→	}
  1498→}
  1499→
  1500→// validateSessionMetadata validates the session-level metadata.json (CommittedMetadata).
  1501→func (env *TestEnv) validateSessionMetadata(v CheckpointValidation) {
  1502→	env.T.Helper()
  1503→
  1504→	metadataPath := SessionMetadataPath(v.CheckpointID)
  1505→	content, found := env.ReadFileFromBranch(paths.MetadataBranchName, metadataPath)
  1506→	if !found {
  1507→		env.T.Fatalf("Session metadata not found at %s", metadataPath)
  1508→	}
  1509→
  1510→	var metadata checkpoint.CommittedMetadata
  1511→	if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(content), &metadata); err != nil {
  1512→		env.T.Fatalf("Failed to parse CommittedMetadata: %v\nContent: %s", err, content)
  1513→	}
  1514→
  1515→	// Validate checkpoint_id
  1516→	if metadata.CheckpointID.String() != v.CheckpointID {
  1517→		env.T.Errorf("CommittedMetadata.CheckpointID = %q, want %q", metadata.CheckpointID, v.CheckpointID)
  1518→	}
  1519→
  1520→	// Validate session_id
  1521→	if v.SessionID != "" && metadata.SessionID != v.SessionID {
  1522→		env.T.Errorf("CommittedMetadata.SessionID = %q, want %q", metadata.SessionID, v.SessionID)
  1523→	}
  1524→
  1525→	// Validate strategy
  1526→	if v.Strategy != "" && metadata.Strategy != v.Strategy {
  1527→		env.T.Errorf("CommittedMetadata.Strategy = %q, want %q", metadata.Strategy, v.Strategy)
  1528→	}
  1529→
  1530→	// Validate created_at is not zero
  1531→	if metadata.CreatedAt.IsZero() {
  1532→		env.T.Error("CommittedMetadata.CreatedAt should not be zero")
  1533→	}
  1534→
  1535→	// Validate files_touched
  1536→	if len(v.FilesTouched) > 0 {
  1537→		touchedSet := make(map[string]bool)
  1538→		for _, f := range metadata.FilesTouched {
  1539→			touchedSet[f] = true
  1540→		}
  1541→		for _, expected := range v.FilesTouched {
  1542→			if !touchedSet[expected] {
  1543→				env.T.Errorf("CommittedMetadata.FilesTouched missing %q, got %v", expected, metadata.FilesTouched)
  1544→			}
  1545→		}
  1546→	}
  1547→
  1548→	// Validate checkpoints_count
  1549→	if v.CheckpointsCount > 0 && metadata.CheckpointsCount != v.CheckpointsCount {

  1554→// validateTranscriptJSONL validates that full.jsonl exists and is valid JSONL.
  1555→func (env *TestEnv) validateTranscriptJSONL(checkpointID string, expectedContent []string) {
  1556→	env.T.Helper()
  1557→
  1558→	transcriptPath := SessionFilePath(checkpointID, paths.TranscriptFileName)
  1559→	content, found := env.ReadFileFromBranch(paths.MetadataBranchName, transcriptPath)
  1560→	if !found {
  1561→		env.T.Fatalf("Transcript not found at %s", transcriptPath)
  1562→	}
  1563→
  1564→	// Validate it's valid JSONL (each non-empty line should be valid JSON)
  1565→	lines := strings.Split(content, "\n")
  1566→	validLines := 0
  1567→	for i, line := range lines {
  1568→		line = strings.TrimSpace(line)
  1569→		if line == "" {
  1570→			continue
  1571→		}
  1572→		validLines++
  1573→		var obj map[string]any
  1574→		if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(line), &obj); err != nil {
  1575→			env.T.Errorf("Transcript line %d is not valid JSON: %v\nLine: %s", i+1, err, line)
  1576→		}
  1577→	}
  1578→
  1579→	if validLines == 0 {
  1580→		env.T.Error("Transcript is empty (no valid JSONL lines)")
  1581→	}
  1582→
  1583→	// Validate expected content appears in transcript
  1584→	for _, expected := range expectedContent {
  1585→		if !strings.Contains(content, expected) {
  1586→			env.T.Errorf("Transcript should contain %q", expected)
  1587→		}
  1588→	}
  1589→}

  1591→// validateContentHash validates that content_hash.txt matches the SHA256 of the transcript.
  1592→func (env *TestEnv) validateContentHash(checkpointID string) {
  1593→	env.T.Helper()
  1594→
  1595→	// Read transcript
  1596→	transcriptPath := SessionFilePath(checkpointID, paths.TranscriptFileName)
  1597→	transcript, found := env.ReadFileFromBranch(paths.MetadataBranchName, transcriptPath)
  1598→	if !found {
  1599→		env.T.Fatalf("Transcript not found at %s", transcriptPath)
  1600→	}
  1601→
  1602→	// Read content hash
  1603→	hashPath := SessionFilePath(checkpointID, "content_hash.txt")
  1604→	storedHash, found := env.ReadFileFromBranch(paths.MetadataBranchName, hashPath)
  1605→	if !found {
  1606→		env.T.Fatalf("Content hash not found at %s", hashPath)
  1607→	}
  1608→	storedHash = strings.TrimSpace(storedHash)
  1609→
  1610→	// Calculate expected hash with sha256: prefix (matches format in committed.go)
  1611→	hash := sha256.Sum256([]byte(transcript))
  1612→	expectedHash := "sha256:" + hex.EncodeToString(hash[:])
  1613→
  1614→	if storedHash != expectedHash {
  1615→		env.T.Errorf("Content hash mismatch:\n  stored:   %s\n  expected: %s", storedHash, expectedHash)
  1616→	}
  1617→}

  1636→func findModuleRoot() string {
  1637→	// Start from this source file's location and walk up to find go.mod
  1638→	_, thisFile, _, ok := runtime.Caller(0)
  1639→	if !ok {
  1640→		panic("failed to get current file path via runtime.Caller")
  1641→	}
  1642→	dir := filepath.Dir(thisFile)
  1643→
  1644→	for {
  1645→		if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(dir, "go.mod")); err == nil {
  1646→			return dir
  1647→		}
  1648→		parent := filepath.Dir(dir)
  1649→		if parent == dir {
  1650→			panic("could not find go.mod starting from " + thisFile)
  1651→		}
  1652→		dir = parent
  1653→	}
  1654→}

   206→func (r *HookRunner) runHookInRepoDir(hookName string, inputJSON []byte) error {
   207→	// Run using the shared test binary
   208→	// Command structure: entire hooks claude-code <hook-name>
   209→	cmd := exec.Command(getTestBinary(), "hooks", "claude-code", hookName)
   210→	cmd.Dir = r.RepoDir
   211→	cmd.Stdin = bytes.NewReader(inputJSON)
   212→	cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(),
   213→		"ENTIRE_TEST_CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR="+r.ClaudeProjectDir,
   214→	)
   215→
   216→	output, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
   217→	if err != nil {
   218→		return fmt.Errorf("hook %s failed: %w\nInput: %s\nOutput: %s",
   219→			hookName, err, inputJSON, output)
   220→	}
   221→
   222→	r.T.Logf("Hook %s output: %s", hookName, output)
   223→	return nil
   224→}

   248→

   256→
   257→// CreateTranscript builds and writes a transcript for the session.
   258→func (s *Session) CreateTranscript(prompt string, changes []FileChange) string {
   259→	s.TranscriptBuilder.AddUserMessage(prompt)
   260→	s.TranscriptBuilder.AddAssistantMessage("I'll help you with that.")
   261→
   262→	for _, change := range changes {
   263→		toolID := s.TranscriptBuilder.AddToolUse("mcp__acp__Write", change.Path, change.Content)
   264→		s.TranscriptBuilder.AddToolResult(toolID)
   265→	}
   266→
   267→	s.TranscriptBuilder.AddAssistantMessage("Done!")
   268→
   269→	if err := s.TranscriptBuilder.WriteToFile(s.TranscriptPath); err != nil {
   270→		s.env.T.Fatalf("failed to write transcript: %v", err)
   271→	}
   272→
   273→	return s.TranscriptPath
   274→}

   512→// NewGeminiHookRunner creates a new Gemini hook runner for the given repo directory.
   513→func NewGeminiHookRunner(repoDir, geminiProjectDir string, t interface {
   514→	Helper()
   515→	Fatalf(format string, args ...interface{})
   516→	Logf(format string, args ...interface{})
   517→}) *GeminiHookRunner {
   518→	return &GeminiHookRunner{

   520→		GeminiProjectDir: geminiProjectDir,

   525→// runGeminiHookWithInput runs a Gemini hook with the given input.
   526→func (r *GeminiHookRunner) runGeminiHookWithInput(hookName string, input interface{}) error {
   527→	r.T.Helper()
   528→
   529→	inputJSON, err := json.Marshal(input)
   530→	if err != nil {
   531→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal hook input: %w", err)
   532→	}
   533→
   534→	return r.runGeminiHookInRepoDir(hookName, inputJSON)
   535→}
   536→
   537→func (r *GeminiHookRunner) runGeminiHookInRepoDir(hookName string, inputJSON []byte) error {
   538→	// Run using the shared test binary
   539→	// Command structure: entire hooks gemini <hook-name>
   540→	cmd := exec.Command(getTestBinary(), "hooks", "gemini", hookName)
   541→	cmd.Dir = r.RepoDir
   542→	cmd.Stdin = bytes.NewReader(inputJSON)
   543→	cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(),
   544→		"ENTIRE_TEST_GEMINI_PROJECT_DIR="+r.GeminiProjectDir,
   545→	)
   546→
   547→	output, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
   548→	if err != nil {
   549→		return fmt.Errorf("hook %s failed: %w\nInput: %s\nOutput: %s",
   550→			hookName, err, inputJSON, output)
   551→	}
   552→
   553→	r.T.Logf("Gemini hook %s output: %s", hookName, output)
   554→	return nil
   555→}
   556→
   557→// runGeminiHookWithOutput runs a Gemini hook and returns both stdout and stderr separately.
   558→func (r *GeminiHookRunner) runGeminiHookWithOutput(hookName string, inputJSON []byte) HookOutput {
   559→	cmd := exec.Command(getTestBinary(), "hooks", "gemini", hookName)
   560→	cmd.Dir = r.RepoDir
   561→	cmd.Stdin = bytes.NewReader(inputJSON)
   562→	cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(),
   563→		"ENTIRE_TEST_GEMINI_PROJECT_DIR="+r.GeminiProjectDir,
   564→	)
   565→
   566→	var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
   567→	cmd.Stdout = &stdout
   568→	cmd.Stderr = &stderr
   569→
   570→	err := cmd.Run()
   571→	return HookOutput{
   572→		Stdout: stdout.Bytes(),
   573→		Stderr: stderr.Bytes(),
   574→		Err:    err,
   575→	}
   576→}

   671→// CreateGeminiTranscript creates a Gemini JSON transcript file for the session.
   672→func (s *GeminiSession) CreateGeminiTranscript(prompt string, changes []FileChange) string {
   673→	// Build Gemini-format transcript (JSON, not JSONL)
   674→	messages := []map[string]interface{}{
   675→		{
   676→			"type":    "user",
   677→			"content": prompt,
   678→		},
   679→		{
   680→			"type":    "assistant",
   681→			"content": "I'll help you with that.",
   682→		},
   683→	}
   684→
   685→	for _, change := range changes {
   686→		messages = append(messages, map[string]interface{}{
   687→			"type": "tool_use",
   688→			"name": "write_file",
   689→			"input": map[string]string{
   690→				"path":    change.Path,
   691→				"content": change.Content,
   692→			},
   693→		})
   694→		messages = append(messages, map[string]interface{}{
   695→			"type":   "tool_result",
   696→			"output": "File written successfully",
   697→		})
   698→	}
   699→
   700→	messages = append(messages, map[string]interface{}{
   701→		"type":    "assistant",
   702→		"content": "Done!",
   703→	})
   704→
   705→	transcript := map[string]interface{}{
   706→		"sessionId": s.ID,
   707→		"messages":  messages,
   708→	}
   709→
   710→	// Ensure directory exists
   711→	if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(s.TranscriptPath), 0o755); err != nil {
   712→		s.env.T.Fatalf("failed to create transcript dir: %v", err)
   713→	}
   714→
   715→	// Write transcript
   716→	data, err := json.MarshalIndent(transcript, "", "  ")
   717→	if err != nil {
   718→		s.env.T.Fatalf("failed to marshal transcript: %v", err)
   719→	}
   720→	if err := os.WriteFile(s.TranscriptPath, data, 0o644); err != nil {
   721→		s.env.T.Fatalf("failed to write transcript: %v", err)
   722→	}
   723→
   724→	return s.TranscriptPath
   725→}

   153→// WriteToFile writes the transcript to a JSONL file.
   154→func (b *TranscriptBuilder) WriteToFile(path string) error {
   155→	// Ensure directory exists
   156→	dir := filepath.Dir(path)
   157→	if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o755); err != nil {
   158→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to create directory: %w", err)
   159→	}
   160→
   161→	file, err := os.Create(path)
   162→	if err != nil {
   163→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to create file: %w", err)
   164→	}
   165→	defer func() { _ = file.Close() }()
   166→
   167→	encoder := json.NewEncoder(file)
   168→	for _, msg := range b.messages {
   169→		if err := encoder.Encode(msg); err != nil {
   170→			return fmt.Errorf("failed to encode message: %w", err)
   171→		}
   172→	}
   173→	return nil
   174→}

   176→// String returns the transcript as a JSONL string.
   177→func (b *TranscriptBuilder) String() string {
   178→	var result string
   179→	var resultSb176 strings.Builder
   180→	for _, msg := range b.messages {
   181→		data, _ := json.Marshal(msg)
   182→		resultSb176.WriteString(string(data) + "\n")
   183→	}
   184→	result += resultSb176.String()
   185→	return result
   186→}

    40→// ParseHookEvent translates OpenCode hook calls into normalized lifecycle events.
    41→func (a *OpenCodeAgent) ParseHookEvent(hookName string, stdin io.Reader) (*agent.Event, error) {
    42→	switch hookName {
    43→	case HookNameSessionStart:
    44→		raw, err := agent.ReadAndParseHookInput[sessionInfoRaw](stdin)
    45→		if err != nil {
    46→			return nil, err
    47→		}

   107→func TestAgentTranscriptRestoration(t *testing.T) {

   314→// stringReader implements io.Reader for test strings
   315→type stringReader struct {
   316→	data []byte
   317→	pos  int
   318→}
   319→
   320→func newStringReader(s string) *stringReader {
   321→	return &stringReader{data: []byte(s)}
   322→}
   323→
   324→func (r *stringReader) Read(p []byte) (n int, err error) {
   325→	if r.pos >= len(r.data) {
   326→		return 0, io.EOF
   327→	}
   328→	n = copy(p, r.data[r.pos:])
   329→	r.pos += n
   330→	return n, nil
   331→}

    89→// TestAgentHookInstallation verifies hook installation via agent interface.
    90→// Note: These tests cannot run in parallel because they use os.Chdir which affects the entire process.
    91→func TestAgentHookInstallation(t *testing.T) {
    92→	// Not parallel - tests use os.Chdir which is process-global
    93→
    94→	t.Run("installs all required hooks", func(t *testing.T) {
    95→		// Not parallel - uses os.Chdir
    96→		env := NewTestEnv(t)
    97→		env.InitRepo()
    98→
    99→		// Change to repo dir
   100→		oldWd, _ := os.Getwd()
   101→		if err := os.Chdir(env.RepoDir); err != nil {
   102→			t.Fatalf("failed to chdir: %v", err)
   103→		}
   104→		defer func() { _ = os.Chdir(oldWd) }()
   105→
   106→		ag, err := agent.Get("claude-code")
   107→		if err != nil {
   108→			t.Fatalf("Get(claude-code) error = %v", err)
   109→		}
   110→
   111→		hookAgent, ok := ag.(agent.HookSupport)
   112→		if !ok {
   113→			t.Fatal("claude-code agent does not implement HookSupport")
   114→		}
   115→
   116→		count, err := hookAgent.InstallHooks(false, false)
   117→		if err != nil {
   118→			t.Fatalf("InstallHooks() error = %v", err)
   119→		}
   120→
   121→		// Should install 7 hooks: SessionStart, SessionEnd, Stop, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse[Task], PostToolUse[Task], PostToolUse[TodoWrite]
   122→		if count != 7 {
   123→			t.Errorf("InstallHooks() count = %d, want 7", count)
   124→		}
   125→
   126→		// Verify hooks are installed
   127→		if !hookAgent.AreHooksInstalled() {
   128→			t.Error("AreHooksInstalled() = false after InstallHooks()")
   129→		}
   130→
   131→		// Verify settings.json was created
   132→		settingsPath := filepath.Join(env.RepoDir, ".claude", claudecode.ClaudeSettingsFileName)
   133→		if _, err := os.Stat(settingsPath); os.IsNotExist(err) {
   134→			t.Error("settings.json was not created")
   135→		}
   136→
   137→		// Verify permissions.deny contains metadata deny rule
   138→		data, err := os.ReadFile(settingsPath)
   139→		if err != nil {
   140→			t.Fatalf("failed to read settings.json: %v", err)
   141→		}
   142→		content := string(data)
   143→		if !strings.Contains(content, "Read(./.entire/metadata/**)") {
   144→			t.Error("settings.json should contain permissions.deny rule for .entire/metadata/**")
   145→		}
   146→	})

   148→	t.Run("idempotent - second install returns 0", func(t *testing.T) {

   153→		oldWd, _ := os.Getwd()

   211→// TestAgentSessionOperations verifies ReadSession/WriteSession via agent interface.
   212→func TestAgentSessionOperations(t *testing.T) {
   213→	t.Parallel()
   214→
   215→	t.Run("ReadSession parses transcript and computes ModifiedFiles", func(t *testing.T) {
   216→		t.Parallel()
   217→		env := NewTestEnv(t)
   218→		env.InitRepo()
   219→
   220→		// Create a transcript file
   221→		transcriptPath := filepath.Join(env.RepoDir, "test-transcript.jsonl")
   222→		transcriptContent := `{"type":"user","uuid":"u1","message":{"content":"Fix the bug"}}
   223→{"type":"assistant","uuid":"a1","message":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"I'll fix it"},{"type":"tool_use","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"main.go"}}]}}
   224→{"type":"user","uuid":"u2","message":{"content":[{"type":"tool_result","tool_use_id":"a1"}]}}
   225→{"type":"assistant","uuid":"a2","message":{"content":[{"type":"tool_use","name":"Edit","input":{"file_path":"util.go"}}]}}
   226→`
   227→		if err := os.WriteFile(transcriptPath, []byte(transcriptContent), 0o644); err != nil {
   228→			t.Fatalf("failed to write transcript: %v", err)
   229→		}
   230→
   231→		ag, _ := agent.Get("claude-code")
   232→		session, err := ag.ReadSession(&agent.HookInput{
   233→			SessionID:  "test-session",
   234→			SessionRef: transcriptPath,
   235→		})
   236→		if err != nil {
   237→			t.Fatalf("ReadSession() error = %v", err)
   238→		}
   239→
   240→		// Verify session metadata
   241→		if session.SessionID != "test-session" {
   242→			t.Errorf("SessionID = %q, want %q", session.SessionID, "test-session")
   243→		}
   244→		if session.AgentName != "claude-code" {
   245→			t.Errorf("AgentName = %q, want %q", session.AgentName, "claude-code")
   246→		}
   247→
   248→		// Verify NativeData is populated
   249→		if len(session.NativeData) == 0 {
   250→			t.Error("NativeData is empty, want transcript content")
   251→		}
   252→
   253→		// Verify ModifiedFiles computed
   254→		if len(session.ModifiedFiles) != 2 {
   255→			t.Errorf("ModifiedFiles = %v, want 2 files (main.go, util.go)", session.ModifiedFiles)
   256→		}
   257→	})
   258→
   259→	t.Run("WriteSession writes NativeData to file", func(t *testing.T) {
   260→		t.Parallel()
   261→		env := NewTestEnv(t)
   262→		env.InitRepo()
   263→
   264→		ag, _ := agent.Get("claude-code")
   265→
   266→		// First read a session
   267→		srcPath := filepath.Join(env.RepoDir, "src.jsonl")
   268→		srcContent := `{"type":"user","uuid":"u1","message":{"content":"hello"}}
   269→`
   270→		if err := os.WriteFile(srcPath, []byte(srcContent), 0o644); err != nil {
   271→			t.Fatalf("failed to write source: %v", err)
   272→		}
   273→
   274→		session, _ := ag.ReadSession(&agent.HookInput{
   275→			SessionID:  "test",
   276→			SessionRef: srcPath,
   277→		})
   278→
   279→		// Write to a new location
   280→		dstPath := filepath.Join(env.RepoDir, "dst.jsonl")
   281→		session.SessionRef = dstPath
   282→
   283→		if err := ag.WriteSession(session); err != nil {
   284→			t.Fatalf("WriteSession() error = %v", err)
   285→		}
   286→
   287→		// Verify file was written
   288→		data, err := os.ReadFile(dstPath)
   289→		if err != nil {
   290→			t.Fatalf("failed to read destination: %v", err)
   291→		}
   292→		if string(data) != srcContent {
   293→			t.Errorf("written content = %q, want %q", string(data), srcContent)
   294→		}
   295→	})
   296→
   297→	t.Run("WriteSession rejects wrong agent", func(t *testing.T) {
   298→		t.Parallel()
   299→
   300→		ag, _ := agent.Get("claude-code")
   301→
   302→		session := &agent.AgentSession{
   303→			SessionID:  "test",
   304→			AgentName:  "other-agent", // Wrong agent
   305→			SessionRef: "/tmp/test.jsonl",
   306→			NativeData: []byte("data"),
   307→		}
   308→
   309→		err := ag.WriteSession(session)
   310→		if err == nil {
   311→			t.Error("WriteSession() should reject session from different agent")
   312→		}
   313→	})
   314→}

   473→// TestGeminiCLIHookInstallation verifies hook installation via Gemini CLI agent interface.
   474→// Note: These tests cannot run in parallel because they use os.Chdir which affects the entire process.
   475→func TestGeminiCLIHookInstallation(t *testing.T) {
   476→	// Not parallel - tests use os.Chdir which is process-global
   477→
   478→	t.Run("installs all required hooks", func(t *testing.T) {
   479→		// Not parallel - uses os.Chdir
   480→		env := NewTestEnv(t)
   481→		env.InitRepo()
   482→
   483→		// Change to repo dir
   484→		oldWd, _ := os.Getwd()
   485→		if err := os.Chdir(env.RepoDir); err != nil {
   486→			t.Fatalf("failed to chdir: %v", err)
   487→		}
   488→		defer func() { _ = os.Chdir(oldWd) }()
   489→
   490→		ag, err := agent.Get("gemini")
   491→		if err != nil {
   492→			t.Fatalf("Get(gemini) error = %v", err)
   493→		}
   494→
   495→		hookAgent, ok := ag.(agent.HookSupport)
   496→		if !ok {
   497→			t.Fatal("gemini agent does not implement HookSupport")
   498→		}
   499→
   500→		count, err := hookAgent.InstallHooks(false, false)
   501→		if err != nil {
   502→			t.Fatalf("InstallHooks() error = %v", err)
   503→		}
   504→
   505→		// Should install 12 hooks: SessionStart, SessionEnd (exit+logout), BeforeAgent, AfterAgent,
   506→		// BeforeModel, AfterModel, BeforeToolSelection, BeforeTool, AfterTool, PreCompress, Notification
   507→		if count != 12 {
   508→			t.Errorf("InstallHooks() count = %d, want 12", count)
   509→		}
   510→
   511→		// Verify hooks are installed
   512→		if !hookAgent.AreHooksInstalled() {
   513→			t.Error("AreHooksInstalled() = false after InstallHooks()")
   514→		}
   515→
   516→		// Verify settings.json was created
   517→		settingsPath := filepath.Join(env.RepoDir, ".gemini", geminicli.GeminiSettingsFileName)
   518→		if _, err := os.Stat(settingsPath); os.IsNotExist(err) {
   519→			t.Error("settings.json was not created")
   520→		}
   521→
   522→		// Verify hooks structure in settings.json
   523→		data, err := os.ReadFile(settingsPath)
   524→		if err != nil {
   525→			t.Fatalf("failed to read settings.json: %v", err)
   526→		}
   527→		content := string(data)
   528→
   529→		// Verify all hook types are present
   530→		if !strings.Contains(content, "SessionStart") {
   531→			t.Error("settings.json should contain SessionStart hook")
   532→		}
   533→		if !strings.Contains(content, "SessionEnd") {
   534→			t.Error("settings.json should contain SessionEnd hook")
   535→		}
   536→		if !strings.Contains(content, "BeforeAgent") {
   537→			t.Error("settings.json should contain BeforeAgent hook")
   538→		}
   539→		if !strings.Contains(content, "AfterAgent") {
   540→			t.Error("settings.json should contain AfterAgent hook")
   541→		}
   542→		if !strings.Contains(content, "BeforeModel") {
   543→			t.Error("settings.json should contain BeforeModel hook")
   544→		}
   545→		if !strings.Contains(content, "AfterModel") {
   546→			t.Error("settings.json should contain AfterModel hook")

    27→// getPluginPath returns the absolute path to the plugin file.
    28→func getPluginPath() (string, error) {
    29→	repoRoot, err := paths.RepoRoot()
    30→	if err != nil {
    31→		// Fallback to CWD if not in a git repo (e.g., during tests)
    32→		//nolint:forbidigo // Intentional fallback when RepoRoot() fails (tests run outside git repos)
    33→		repoRoot, err = os.Getwd()
    34→		if err != nil {
    35→			return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to get current directory: %w", err)
    36→		}
    37→	}
    38→	return filepath.Join(repoRoot, ".opencode", pluginDirName, pluginFileName), nil
    39→}
    40→
    41→// InstallHooks writes the Entire plugin file to .opencode/plugins/entire.ts.
    42→// Returns 1 if the plugin was installed, 0 if already present (idempotent).
    43→func (a *OpenCodeAgent) InstallHooks(localDev bool, force bool) (int, error) {
    44→	pluginPath, err := getPluginPath()
    45→	if err != nil {
    46→		return 0, err
    47→	}
    48→
    49→	// Check if already installed (idempotent) unless force
    50→	if !force {
    51→		if _, err := os.Stat(pluginPath); err == nil {
    52→			data, readErr := os.ReadFile(pluginPath) //nolint:gosec // Path constructed from repo root
    53→			if readErr == nil && strings.Contains(string(data), entireMarker) {
    54→				return 0, nil // Already installed
    55→			}
    56→		}
    57→	}
    58→
    59→	// Build the command prefix
    60→	var cmdPrefix string
    61→	if localDev {
    62→		cmdPrefix = "go run ${OPENCODE_PROJECT_DIR}/cmd/entire/main.go"
    63→	} else {
    64→		cmdPrefix = "entire"
    65→	}
    66→
    67→	// Generate plugin content from template
    68→	content := strings.ReplaceAll(pluginTemplate, entireCmdPlaceholder, cmdPrefix)
    69→
    70→	// Ensure directory exists
    71→	pluginDir := filepath.Dir(pluginPath)
    72→	//nolint:gosec // G301: Plugin directory needs standard permissions
    73→	if err := os.MkdirAll(pluginDir, 0o755); err != nil {
    74→		return 0, fmt.Errorf("failed to create plugin directory: %w", err)
    75→	}
    76→
    77→	// Write plugin file
    78→	//nolint:gosec // G306: Plugin file needs standard permissions for OpenCode to read
    79→	if err := os.WriteFile(pluginPath, []byte(content), 0o644); err != nil {
    80→		return 0, fmt.Errorf("failed to write plugin file: %w", err)
    81→	}
    82→
    83→	return 1, nil
    84→}

    86→// UninstallHooks removes the Entire plugin file.
    87→func (a *OpenCodeAgent) UninstallHooks() error {
    88→	pluginPath, err := getPluginPath()
    89→	if err != nil {
    90→		return err
    91→	}
    92→
    93→	if err := os.Remove(pluginPath); err != nil && !os.IsNotExist(err) {
    94→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to remove plugin file: %w", err)
    95→	}
    96→
    97→	return nil
    98→}

   100→// AreHooksInstalled checks if the Entire plugin file exists and contains the marker.
   101→func (a *OpenCodeAgent) AreHooksInstalled() bool {
   102→	pluginPath, err := getPluginPath()
   103→	if err != nil {
   104→		return false
   105→	}
   106→
   107→	data, err := os.ReadFile(pluginPath) //nolint:gosec // Path constructed from repo root
   108→	if err != nil {

   110→	}
   111→

   115→// GetSupportedHooks returns the normalized lifecycle events this agent supports.
   116→// OpenCode's native hooks map to standard agent lifecycle events:
   117→//   - session-start → HookSessionStart
   118→//   - session-end   → HookSessionEnd
   119→//   - turn-start    → HookUserPromptSubmit (user prompt triggers a turn)
   120→//   - turn-end      → HookStop (agent response complete)
   121→//
   122→// Note: HookNames() returns 5 hooks (including "compaction"), but GetSupportedHooks()
   123→// returns only 4. The "compaction" hook is OpenCode-specific with no standard HookType
   124→// mapping — it is handled via ParseHookEvent but not advertised as a standard lifecycle event.
   125→func (a *OpenCodeAgent) GetSupportedHooks() []agent.HookType {
   126→	return []agent.HookType{
   127→		agent.HookSessionStart,
   128→		agent.HookSessionEnd,
   129→		agent.HookUserPromptSubmit,
   130→		agent.HookStop,
   131→	}

   100→// loadFromFile loads settings from a specific file path.
   101→// Returns default settings if the file doesn't exist.
   102→func loadFromFile(filePath string) (*EntireSettings, error) {
   103→	settings := &EntireSettings{
   104→		Strategy: DefaultStrategyName,
   105→		Enabled:  true, // Default to enabled
   106→	}
   107→
   108→	data, err := os.ReadFile(filePath) //nolint:gosec // path is from caller
   109→	if err != nil {
   110→		if os.IsNotExist(err) {
   111→			return settings, nil
   112→		}
   113→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w", err)
   114→	}
   115→
   116→	dec := json.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(data))
   117→	dec.DisallowUnknownFields()
   118→	if err := dec.Decode(settings); err != nil {
   119→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("parsing settings file: %w", err)
   120→	}
   121→	applyDefaults(settings)
   122→
   123→	return settings, nil
   124→}
   125→
   126→// mergeJSON merges JSON data into existing settings.
   127→// Only non-zero values from the JSON override existing settings.
   128→func mergeJSON(settings *EntireSettings, data []byte) error {
   129→	// First, validate that there are no unknown keys using strict decoding
   130→	dec := json.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(data))
   131→	dec.DisallowUnknownFields()
   132→	var temp EntireSettings
   133→	if err := dec.Decode(&temp); err != nil {
   134→		return fmt.Errorf("parsing JSON: %w", err)
   135→	}
   136→
   137→	// Parse into a map to check which fields are present
   138→	var raw map[string]json.RawMessage
   139→	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &raw); err != nil {
   140→		return fmt.Errorf("parsing JSON: %w", err)
   141→	}
   142→
   143→	// Override strategy if present and non-empty
   144→	if strategyRaw, ok := raw["strategy"]; ok {
   145→		var s string
   146→		if err := json.Unmarshal(strategyRaw, &s); err != nil {
   147→			return fmt.Errorf("parsing strategy field: %w", err)
   148→		}
   149→		if s != "" {
   150→			settings.Strategy = s
   151→		}
   152→	}
   153→
   154→	// Override enabled if present
   155→	if enabledRaw, ok := raw["enabled"]; ok {
   156→		var e bool
   157→		if err := json.Unmarshal(enabledRaw, &e); err != nil {
   158→			return fmt.Errorf("parsing enabled field: %w", err)
   159→		}
   160→		settings.Enabled = e
   161→	}
   162→
   163→	// Override local_dev if present
   164→	if localDevRaw, ok := raw["local_dev"]; ok {
   165→		var ld bool
   166→		if err := json.Unmarshal(localDevRaw, &ld); err != nil {
   167→			return fmt.Errorf("parsing local_dev field: %w", err)
   168→		}
   169→		settings.LocalDev = ld
   170→	}
   171→
   172→	// Override log_level if present and non-empty
   173→	if logLevelRaw, ok := raw["log_level"]; ok {
   174→		var ll string
   175→		if err := json.Unmarshal(logLevelRaw, &ll); err != nil {
   176→			return fmt.Errorf("parsing log_level field: %w", err)
   177→		}
   178→		if ll != "" {
   179→			settings.LogLevel = ll
   180→		}
   181→	}
   182→
   183→	// Merge strategy_options if present
   184→	if optionsRaw, ok := raw["strategy_options"]; ok {
   185→		var opts map[string]any
   186→		if err := json.Unmarshal(optionsRaw, &opts); err != nil {
   187→			return fmt.Errorf("parsing strategy_options field: %w", err)
   188→		}
   189→		if settings.StrategyOptions == nil {
   190→			settings.StrategyOptions = opts
   191→		} else {
   192→			for k, v := range opts {
   193→				settings.StrategyOptions[k] = v
   194→			}
   195→		}
   196→	}
   197→
   198→	// Override telemetry if present
   199→	if telemetryRaw, ok := raw["telemetry"]; ok {
   200→		var t bool
   201→		if err := json.Unmarshal(telemetryRaw, &t); err != nil {
   202→			return fmt.Errorf("parsing telemetry field: %w", err)
   203→		}
   204→		settings.Telemetry = &t
   205→	}
   206→
   207→	return nil
   208→}

   210→func applyDefaults(settings *EntireSettings) {
   211→	if settings.Strategy == "" {
   212→		settings.Strategy = DefaultStrategyName
   213→	}
   214→}
   215→
   216→// IsSummarizeEnabled checks if auto-summarize is enabled in settings.
   217→// Returns false by default if settings cannot be loaded or the key is missing.
   218→func IsSummarizeEnabled() bool {
   219→	settings, err := Load()
   220→	if err != nil {
   221→		return false
   222→	}
   223→	return settings.IsSummarizeEnabled()
   224→}
   225→
   226→// IsSummarizeEnabled checks if auto-summarize is enabled in this settings instance.
   227→func (s *EntireSettings) IsSummarizeEnabled() bool {
   228→	if s.StrategyOptions == nil {
   229→		return false
   230→	}
   231→	summarizeOpts, ok := s.StrategyOptions["summarize"].(map[string]any)
   232→	if !ok {
   233→		return false
   234→	}
   235→	enabled, ok := summarizeOpts["enabled"].(bool)
   236→	if !ok {
   237→		return false
   238→	}
   239→	return enabled
   240→}
   241→
   242→// IsPushSessionsDisabled checks if push_sessions is disabled in settings.
   243→// Returns true if push_sessions is explicitly set to false.
   244→func (s *EntireSettings) IsPushSessionsDisabled() bool {
   245→	if s.StrategyOptions == nil {
   246→		return false
   247→	}
   248→	val, exists := s.StrategyOptions["push_sessions"]
   249→	if !exists {
   250→		return false
   251→	}
   252→	if boolVal, ok := val.(bool); ok {
   253→		return !boolVal // disabled = !push_sessions
   254→	}
   255→	return false
   256→}

   267→
   268→// saveToFile saves settings to the specified file path.
   269→func saveToFile(settings *EntireSettings, filePath string) error {
   270→	// Get absolute path for the file
   271→	filePathAbs, err := paths.AbsPath(filePath)
   272→	if err != nil {
   273→		filePathAbs = filePath // Fallback to relative
   274→	}
   275→
   276→	// Ensure directory exists
   277→	dir := filepath.Dir(filePathAbs)
   278→	if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o750); err != nil {
   279→		return fmt.Errorf("creating settings directory: %w", err)
   280→	}

   282→	data, err := jsonutil.MarshalIndentWithNewline(settings, "", "  ")
   283→	if err != nil {

   285→	}
   286→
   287→	//nolint:gosec // G306: settings file is config, not secrets; 0o644 is appropriate
   288→	if err := os.WriteFile(filePathAbs, data, 0o644); err != nil {
   289→		return fmt.Errorf("writing settings file: %w", err)
   290→	}
   291→	return nil
   292→}

   101→			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to parse hook response: %w\nStdout: %s",
   102→				err, output.Stdout)
   103→		}
   104→	}
   105→
   106→	return &resp, nil
   107→}

   207→func (r *HookRunner) runHookInRepoDir(hookName string, inputJSON []byte) error {
   208→	// Run using the shared test binary
   209→	// Command structure: entire hooks claude-code <hook-name>
   210→	cmd := exec.Command(getTestBinary(), "hooks", "claude-code", hookName)
   211→	cmd.Dir = r.RepoDir
   212→	cmd.Stdin = bytes.NewReader(inputJSON)
   213→	cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(),
   214→		"ENTIRE_TEST_CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR="+r.ClaudeProjectDir,
   215→	)
   216→
   217→	output, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
   218→	if err != nil {
   219→		return fmt.Errorf("hook %s failed: %w\nInput: %s\nOutput: %s",
   220→			hookName, err, inputJSON, output)
   221→	}
   222→
   223→	r.T.Logf("Hook %s output: %s", hookName, output)
   224→	return nil
   225→}

   227→// Session represents a simulated Claude Code session.
   228→type Session struct {
   229→	ID                string // Raw model session ID (e.g., "test-session-1")
   230→	TranscriptPath    string
   231→	TranscriptBuilder *TranscriptBuilder
   232→	env               *TestEnv
   233→}
   234→
   235→// FileChange represents a file modification in a session.
   236→type FileChange struct {
   237→	Path    string
   238→	Content string
   239→}
   240→
   241→// NewSession creates a new simulated session.
   242→func (env *TestEnv) NewSession() *Session {
   243→	env.T.Helper()
   244→
   245→	env.SessionCounter++
   246→	sessionID := fmt.Sprintf("test-session-%d", env.SessionCounter)
   247→
   248→	transcriptPath := filepath.Join(env.RepoDir, ".entire", "tmp", sessionID+".jsonl")
   249→
   250→	return &Session{
   251→		ID:                sessionID,
   252→		TranscriptPath:    transcriptPath,
   253→		TranscriptBuilder: NewTranscriptBuilder(),
   254→		env:               env,
   255→	}
   256→}
   257→
   258→// CreateTranscript builds and writes a transcript for the session.
   259→func (s *Session) CreateTranscript(prompt string, changes []FileChange) string {
   260→	s.TranscriptBuilder.AddUserMessage(prompt)
   261→	s.TranscriptBuilder.AddAssistantMessage("I'll help you with that.")
   262→
   263→	for _, change := range changes {
   264→		toolID := s.TranscriptBuilder.AddToolUse("mcp__acp__Write", change.Path, change.Content)
   265→		s.TranscriptBuilder.AddToolResult(toolID)
   266→	}
   267→
   268→	s.TranscriptBuilder.AddAssistantMessage("Done!")
   269→
   270→	if err := s.TranscriptBuilder.WriteToFile(s.TranscriptPath); err != nil {
   271→		s.env.T.Fatalf("failed to write transcript: %v", err)
   272→	}
   273→
   274→	return s.TranscriptPath
   275→}

   367→// ClearSessionState removes the session state file for the given session ID.
   368→// This simulates what happens when a user commits their changes (session is "completed").
   369→// Used in tests to allow sequential sessions to run without triggering concurrent session warnings.
   370→func (env *TestEnv) ClearSessionState(sessionID string) error {
   371→	env.T.Helper()
   372→
   373→	// Session state is stored in .git/entire-sessions/<session-id>.json
   374→	stateFile := filepath.Join(env.RepoDir, ".git", "entire-sessions", sessionID+".json")
   375→
   376→	if err := os.Remove(stateFile); err != nil && !os.IsNotExist(err) {
   377→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to clear session state: %w", err)
   378→	}
   379→	return nil
   380→}

   382→// HookOutput contains the result of running a hook.
   383→type HookOutput struct {
   384→	Stdout []byte
   385→	Stderr []byte
   386→	Err    error
   387→}
   388→
   389→// runHookWithOutput runs a hook and returns both stdout and stderr separately.
   390→func (r *HookRunner) runHookWithOutput(hookName string, inputJSON []byte) HookOutput {
   391→	cmd := exec.Command(getTestBinary(), "hooks", "claude-code", hookName)
   392→	cmd.Dir = r.RepoDir
   393→	cmd.Stdin = bytes.NewReader(inputJSON)
   394→	cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(),
   395→		"ENTIRE_TEST_CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR="+r.ClaudeProjectDir,
   396→	)
   397→
   398→	var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
   399→	cmd.Stdout = &stdout
   400→	cmd.Stderr = &stderr
   401→
   402→	err := cmd.Run()
   403→	return HookOutput{
   404→		Stdout: stdout.Bytes(),
   405→		Stderr: stderr.Bytes(),
   406→		Err:    err,
   407→	}
   408→}

   458→// GetSessionState reads and returns the session state for the given session ID.
   459→func (env *TestEnv) GetSessionState(sessionID string) (*strategy.SessionState, error) {
   460→	env.T.Helper()
   461→
   462→	stateFile := filepath.Join(env.RepoDir, ".git", "entire-sessions", sessionID+".json")
   463→
   464→	data, err := os.ReadFile(stateFile)
   465→	if os.IsNotExist(err) {
   466→		return nil, nil
   467→	}
   468→	if err != nil {
   469→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read session state: %w", err)
   470→	}
   471→
   472→	var state strategy.SessionState
   473→	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &state); err != nil {
   474→		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to parse session state: %w", err)
   475→	}
   476→	return &state, nil
   477→}
   478→
   479→// WriteSessionState writes the session state for the given session ID.
   480→// This is useful for tests that need to manipulate session state directly.
   481→func (env *TestEnv) WriteSessionState(sessionID string, state *strategy.SessionState) error {
   482→	env.T.Helper()
   483→
   484→	stateDir := filepath.Join(env.RepoDir, ".git", "entire-sessions")
   485→	if err := os.MkdirAll(stateDir, 0o755); err != nil {
   486→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to create session state dir: %w", err)
   487→	}
   488→
   489→	stateFile := filepath.Join(stateDir, sessionID+".json")
   490→
   491→	data, err := json.MarshalIndent(state, "", "  ")
   492→	if err != nil {
   493→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal session state: %w", err)
   494→	}
   495→
   496→	if err := os.WriteFile(stateFile, data, 0o644); err != nil {
   497→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to write session state: %w", err)
   498→	}
   499→	return nil
   500→}

   657→// NewGeminiSession creates a new simulated Gemini session.
   658→func (env *TestEnv) NewGeminiSession() *GeminiSession {
   659→	env.T.Helper()

   662→	sessionID := fmt.Sprintf("gemini-session-%d", env.SessionCounter)
   663→	transcriptPath := filepath.Join(env.RepoDir, ".entire", "tmp", sessionID+".json")
   664→
   665→	return &GeminiSession{

   672→// CreateGeminiTranscript creates a Gemini JSON transcript file for the session.
   673→func (s *GeminiSession) CreateGeminiTranscript(prompt string, changes []FileChange) string {
   674→	// Build Gemini-format transcript (JSON, not JSONL)
   675→	messages := []map[string]interface{}{
   676→		{
   677→			"type":    "user",
   678→			"content": prompt,
   679→		},
   680→		{
   681→			"type":    "assistant",
   682→			"content": "I'll help you with that.",
   683→		},
   684→	}
   685→
   686→	for _, change := range changes {
   687→		messages = append(messages, map[string]interface{}{
   688→			"type": "tool_use",
   689→			"name": "write_file",
   690→			"input": map[string]string{
   691→				"path":    change.Path,
   692→				"content": change.Content,
   693→			},
   694→		})
   695→		messages = append(messages, map[string]interface{}{
   696→			"type":   "tool_result",
   697→			"output": "File written successfully",
   698→		})
   699→	}
   700→
   701→	messages = append(messages, map[string]interface{}{
   702→		"type":    "assistant",
   703→		"content": "Done!",
   704→	})
   705→
   706→	transcript := map[string]interface{}{
   707→		"sessionId": s.ID,
   708→		"messages":  messages,
   709→	}
   710→
   711→	// Ensure directory exists
   712→	if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(s.TranscriptPath), 0o755); err != nil {
   713→		s.env.T.Fatalf("failed to create transcript dir: %v", err)
   714→	}
   715→
   716→	// Write transcript
   717→	data, err := json.MarshalIndent(transcript, "", "  ")
   718→	if err != nil {
   719→		s.env.T.Fatalf("failed to marshal transcript: %v", err)
   720→	}
   721→	if err := os.WriteFile(s.TranscriptPath, data, 0o644); err != nil {
   722→		s.env.T.Fatalf("failed to write transcript: %v", err)
   723→	}
   724→
   725→	return s.TranscriptPath
   726→}

   769→// NewOpenCodeHookRunner creates a new OpenCode hook runner for the given repo directory.
   770→func NewOpenCodeHookRunner(repoDir, openCodeProjectDir string, t interface {
   771→	Helper()
   772→	Fatalf(format string, args ...interface{})
   773→	Logf(format string, args ...interface{})
   774→}) *OpenCodeHookRunner {

   782→func (r *OpenCodeHookRunner) runOpenCodeHookWithInput(hookName string, input interface{}) error {
   783→	r.T.Helper()
   784→
   785→	inputJSON, err := json.Marshal(input)
   786→	if err != nil {
   787→		return fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal hook input: %w", err)
   788→	}
   789→
   790→	return r.runOpenCodeHookInRepoDir(hookName, inputJSON)
   791→}
   792→
   793→func (r *OpenCodeHookRunner) runOpenCodeHookInRepoDir(hookName string, inputJSON []byte) error {
   794→	// Command structure: entire hooks opencode <hook-name>
   795→	cmd := exec.Command(getTestBinary(), "hooks", "opencode", hookName)
   796→	cmd.Dir = r.RepoDir
   797→	cmd.Stdin = bytes.NewReader(inputJSON)
   798→	cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(),
   799→		"ENTIRE_TEST_OPENCODE_PROJECT_DIR="+r.OpenCodeProjectDir,
   800→	)
   801→
   802→	output, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
   803→	if err != nil {
   804→		return fmt.Errorf("hook %s failed: %w\nInput: %s\nOutput: %s",
   805→			hookName, err, inputJSON, output)
   806→	}
   807→
   808→	r.T.Logf("OpenCode hook %s output: %s", hookName, output)
   809→	return nil
   810→}

   871→// NewOpenCodeSession creates a new simulated OpenCode session.
   872→func (env *TestEnv) NewOpenCodeSession() *OpenCodeSession {
   873→	env.T.Helper()
   874→
   875→	env.SessionCounter++
   876→	sessionID := fmt.Sprintf("opencode-session-%d", env.SessionCounter)
   877→	transcriptPath := filepath.Join(env.OpenCodeProjectDir, sessionID+".jsonl")
   878→
   879→	return &OpenCodeSession{

   881→		TranscriptPath: transcriptPath,

   883→	}
   884→}

   886→// CreateOpenCodeTranscript creates an OpenCode JSONL transcript file for the session.
   887→// Each line is a JSON message in OpenCode's format (id, role, content, time, tokens, parts).
   888→func (s *OpenCodeSession) CreateOpenCodeTranscript(prompt string, changes []FileChange) string {
   889→	var lines []string
   890→
   891→	// User message
   892→	s.msgCounter++
   893→	userMsg := map[string]interface{}{
   894→		"id":      fmt.Sprintf("msg-%d", s.msgCounter),
   895→		"role":    "user",
   896→		"content": prompt,
   897→		"time":    map[string]interface{}{"created": 1708300000 + s.msgCounter},
   898→	}
   899→	userJSON, _ := json.Marshal(userMsg)
   900→	lines = append(lines, string(userJSON))
   901→
   902→	// Assistant message with tool calls for file changes
   903→	s.msgCounter++
   904→	var parts []map[string]interface{}
   905→	parts = append(parts, map[string]interface{}{
   906→		"type": "text",
   907→		"text": "I'll help you with that.",
   908→	})
   909→	for i, change := range changes {
   910→		parts = append(parts, map[string]interface{}{
   911→			"type":   "tool",
   912→			"tool":   "write",
   913→			"callID": fmt.Sprintf("call-%d", i+1),
   914→			"state": map[string]interface{}{
   915→				"status": "completed",
   916→				"input":  map[string]string{"file_path": change.Path},
   917→				"output": "File written: " + change.Path,
   918→			},
   919→		})
   920→	}
   921→
   922→	asstMsg := map[string]interface{}{
   923→		"id":      fmt.Sprintf("msg-%d", s.msgCounter),
   924→		"role":    "assistant",
   925→		"content": "Done!",
   926→		"time": map[string]interface{}{
   927→			"created":   1708300000 + s.msgCounter,
   928→			"completed": 1708300000 + s.msgCounter + 5,
   929→		},
   930→		"tokens": map[string]interface{}{
   931→			"input":     150,
   932→			"output":    80,
   933→			"reasoning": 10,
   934→			"cache":     map[string]int{"read": 5, "write": 15},
   935→		},
   936→		"cost":  0.003,
   937→		"parts": parts,
   938→	}
   939→	asstJSON, _ := json.Marshal(asstMsg)
   940→	lines = append(lines, string(asstJSON))
   941→
   942→	// Ensure directory exists
   943→	if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(s.TranscriptPath), 0o755); err != nil {
   944→		s.env.T.Fatalf("failed to create transcript dir: %v", err)
   945→	}
   946→
   947→	// Write JSONL transcript (one message per line)
   948→	content := strings.Join(lines, "\n") + "\n"
   949→	if err := os.WriteFile(s.TranscriptPath, []byte(content), 0o644); err != nil {
   950→		s.env.T.Fatalf("failed to write transcript: %v", err)
   951→	}
   952→
   953→	return s.TranscriptPath
   954→}

   960→	return runner.SimulateOpenCodeSessionStart(sessionID, transcriptPath)

    13→// TestOpenCodeHookFlow verifies the full hook flow for OpenCode:
    14→// session-start → turn-start → file changes → turn-end → checkpoint → commit → condense → session-end.
    15→func TestOpenCodeHookFlow(t *testing.T) {
    16→	t.Parallel()
    17→
    18→	RunForAllStrategies(t, func(t *testing.T, env *TestEnv, strategyName string) {
    19→		env.InitEntireWithAgent(strategyName, agent.AgentNameOpenCode)
    20→
    21→		// Create OpenCode session
    22→		session := env.NewOpenCodeSession()
    23→
    24→		// 1. session-start
    25→		if err := env.SimulateOpenCodeSessionStart(session.ID, session.TranscriptPath); err != nil {
    26→			t.Fatalf("session-start error: %v", err)
    27→		}
    28→
    29→		// 2. turn-start (equivalent to UserPromptSubmit)
    30→		if err := env.SimulateOpenCodeTurnStart(session.ID, session.TranscriptPath, "Add a feature"); err != nil {
    31→			t.Fatalf("turn-start error: %v", err)
    32→		}
    33→
    34→		// 3. Agent makes file changes
    35→		env.WriteFile("feature.go", "package main\n// new feature")
    36→
    37→		// 4. Create transcript with the file change
    38→		session.CreateOpenCodeTranscript("Add a feature", []FileChange{
    39→			{Path: "feature.go", Content: "package main\n// new feature"},
    40→		})
    41→
    42→		// 5. turn-end (equivalent to Stop — creates checkpoint)
    43→		if err := env.SimulateOpenCodeTurnEnd(session.ID, session.TranscriptPath); err != nil {
    44→			t.Fatalf("turn-end error: %v", err)
    45→		}
    46→
    47→		// 6. Verify checkpoint was created
    48→		points := env.GetRewindPoints()
    49→		if len(points) == 0 {
    50→			t.Fatal("expected at least 1 rewind point after turn-end")
    51→		}
    52→
    53→		// 7. Commit (triggers condensation for manual-commit strategy)
    54→		env.WriteFile("feature.go", "package main\n// new feature\n// committed")
    55→		env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Add feature", "feature.go")
    56→
    57→		// 8. session-end
    58→		if err := env.SimulateOpenCodeSessionEnd(session.ID, session.TranscriptPath); err != nil {
    59→			t.Fatalf("session-end error: %v", err)
    60→		}
    61→
    62→		// 9. Verify condensation happened (checkpoint on metadata branch)
    63→		checkpointID := env.TryGetLatestCheckpointID()
    64→		if checkpointID == "" {
    65→			t.Fatal("expected checkpoint on metadata branch after commit")
    66→		}
    67→
    68→		// 10. Verify condensed data
    69→		transcriptPath := SessionFilePath(checkpointID, paths.TranscriptFileName)
    70→		_, found := env.ReadFileFromBranch(paths.MetadataBranchName, transcriptPath)
    71→		if !found {
    72→			t.Error("condensed transcript should exist on metadata branch")
    73→		}
    74→	})
    75→}

   140→func TestOpenCodeRewind(t *testing.T) {

   185→	if err := env.SimulateOpenCodeTurnEnd(session.ID, session.TranscriptPath); err != nil {

   212→// TestOpenCodeMultiTurnCondensation verifies that multiple turns in a session
   213→// are correctly condensed when the user commits.
   214→func TestOpenCodeMultiTurnCondensation(t *testing.T) {
   215→	t.Parallel()
   216→
   217→	env := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t, strategy.StrategyNameManualCommit)
   218→	env.InitEntireWithAgent(strategy.StrategyNameManualCommit, agent.AgentNameOpenCode)
   219→
   220→	session := env.NewOpenCodeSession()
   221→	transcriptPath := session.TranscriptPath
   222→
   223→	// session-start
   224→	if err := env.SimulateOpenCodeSessionStart(session.ID, transcriptPath); err != nil {
   225→		t.Fatalf("session-start error: %v", err)
   226→	}
   227→
   228→	// Turn 1: create file
   229→	env.WriteFile("app.go", "package main\nfunc main() {}")
   230→	session.CreateOpenCodeTranscript("Create app.go", []FileChange{
   231→		{Path: "app.go", Content: "package main\nfunc main() {}"},
   232→	})
   233→
   234→	if err := env.SimulateOpenCodeTurnStart(session.ID, transcriptPath, "Create app.go"); err != nil {
   235→		t.Fatalf("turn-start error: %v", err)
   236→	}
   237→	if err := env.SimulateOpenCodeTurnEnd(session.ID, transcriptPath); err != nil {
   238→		t.Fatalf("turn-end error: %v", err)
   239→	}
   240→
   241→	// Verify checkpoint
   242→	points := env.GetRewindPoints()
   243→	if len(points) == 0 {
   244→		t.Fatal("expected rewind point after first turn")
   245→	}
   246→
   247→	// Commit with hooks (triggers condensation)
   248→	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Implement app", "app.go")
   249→
   250→	// session-end
   251→	if err := env.SimulateOpenCodeSessionEnd(session.ID, transcriptPath); err != nil {
   252→		t.Fatalf("session-end error: %v", err)
   253→	}
   254→
   255→	// Verify checkpoint was condensed to metadata branch
   256→	checkpointID := env.TryGetLatestCheckpointID()
   257→	if checkpointID == "" {
   258→		t.Fatal("expected checkpoint on metadata branch after commit")
   259→	}
   260→
   261→	// Verify files are on metadata branch
   262→	env.ValidateCheckpoint(CheckpointValidation{
   263→		CheckpointID: checkpointID,
   264→		Strategy:     strategy.StrategyNameManualCommit,
   265→		FilesTouched: []string{"app.go"},
   266→		ExpectedTranscriptContent: []string{
   267→			"Create app.go", // User prompt should appear in transcript
   268→		},
   269→	})
   270→}

   474→// TestGeminiCLIHookInstallation verifies hook installation via Gemini CLI agent interface.
   475→// Note: These tests cannot run in parallel because they use os.Chdir which affects the entire process.
   476→func TestGeminiCLIHookInstallation(t *testing.T) {
   477→	// Not parallel - tests use os.Chdir which is process-global
   478→
   479→	t.Run("installs all required hooks", func(t *testing.T) {
   480→		// Not parallel - uses os.Chdir
   481→		env := NewTestEnv(t)
   482→		env.InitRepo()
   483→
   484→		// Change to repo dir
   485→		oldWd, _ := os.Getwd()
   486→		if err := os.Chdir(env.RepoDir); err != nil {
   487→			t.Fatalf("failed to chdir: %v", err)
   488→		}
   489→		defer func() { _ = os.Chdir(oldWd) }()
   490→
   491→		ag, err := agent.Get("gemini")
   492→		if err != nil {
   493→			t.Fatalf("Get(gemini) error = %v", err)
   494→		}
   495→
   496→		hookAgent, ok := ag.(agent.HookSupport)
   497→		if !ok {
   498→			t.Fatal("gemini agent does not implement HookSupport")
   499→		}
   500→
   501→		count, err := hookAgent.InstallHooks(false, false)
   502→		if err != nil {
   503→			t.Fatalf("InstallHooks() error = %v", err)
   504→		}
   505→
   506→		// Should install 12 hooks: SessionStart, SessionEnd (exit+logout), BeforeAgent, AfterAgent,
   507→		// BeforeModel, AfterModel, BeforeToolSelection, BeforeTool, AfterTool, PreCompress, Notification
   508→		if count != 12 {
   509→			t.Errorf("InstallHooks() count = %d, want 12", count)
   510→		}
   511→
   512→		// Verify hooks are installed
   513→		if !hookAgent.AreHooksInstalled() {
   514→			t.Error("AreHooksInstalled() = false after InstallHooks()")
   515→		}
   516→
   517→		// Verify settings.json was created
   518→		settingsPath := filepath.Join(env.RepoDir, ".gemini", geminicli.GeminiSettingsFileName)
   519→		if _, err := os.Stat(settingsPath); os.IsNotExist(err) {
   520→			t.Error("settings.json was not created")
   521→		}
   522→
   523→		// Verify hooks structure in settings.json
   524→		data, err := os.ReadFile(settingsPath)
   525→		if err != nil {
   526→			t.Fatalf("failed to read settings.json: %v", err)
   527→		}
   528→		content := string(data)
   529→
   530→		// Verify all hook types are present
   531→		if !strings.Contains(content, "SessionStart") {
   532→			t.Error("settings.json should contain SessionStart hook")
   533→		}
   534→		if !strings.Contains(content, "SessionEnd") {
   535→			t.Error("settings.json should contain SessionEnd hook")
   536→		}
   537→		if !strings.Contains(content, "BeforeAgent") {
   538→			t.Error("settings.json should contain BeforeAgent hook")
   539→		}
   540→		if !strings.Contains(content, "AfterAgent") {
   541→			t.Error("settings.json should contain AfterAgent hook")
   542→		}
   543→		if !strings.Contains(content, "BeforeModel") {
   544→			t.Error("settings.json should contain BeforeModel hook")
   545→		}
   546→		if !strings.Contains(content, "AfterModel") {
   547→			t.Error("settings.json should contain AfterModel hook")
   548→		}
   549→		if !strings.Contains(content, "BeforeToolSelection") {
   550→			t.Error("settings.json should contain BeforeToolSelection hook")
   551→		}
   552→		if !strings.Contains(content, "BeforeTool") {
   553→			t.Error("settings.json should contain BeforeTool hook")
   554→		}
   555→		if !strings.Contains(content, "AfterTool") {
   556→			t.Error("settings.json should contain AfterTool hook")
   557→		}
   558→		if !strings.Contains(content, "PreCompress") {
   559→			t.Error("settings.json should contain PreCompress hook")
   560→		}
   561→		if !strings.Contains(content, "Notification") {
   562→			t.Error("settings.json should contain Notification hook")
   563→		}
   564→
   565→		// Verify hooksConfig is set
   566→		if !strings.Contains(content, "hooksConfig") {
   567→			t.Error("settings.json should contain hooksConfig.enabled")
   568→		}
   569→	})
   570→
   571→	t.Run("idempotent - second install returns 0", func(t *testing.T) {
   572→		// Not parallel - uses os.Chdir

   699→// TestGeminiCLISessionOperations verifies ReadSession/WriteSession via Gemini agent interface.
   700→func TestGeminiCLISessionOperations(t *testing.T) {
   701→	t.Parallel()
   702→
   703→	t.Run("ReadSession parses transcript and computes ModifiedFiles", func(t *testing.T) {
   704→		t.Parallel()
   705→		env := NewTestEnv(t)
   706→		env.InitRepo()
   707→
   708→		// Create a Gemini transcript file (JSON format)
   709→		// Gemini uses "type" field with values "user" or "gemini", and "toolCalls" array with "args"
   710→		transcriptPath := filepath.Join(env.RepoDir, "test-transcript.json")
   711→		transcriptContent := `{
   712→  "messages": [
   713→    {"type": "user", "content": "Fix the bug"},
   714→    {"type": "gemini", "content": "", "toolCalls": [{"name": "write_file", "args": {"file_path": "main.go"}}]},
   715→    {"type": "gemini", "content": "", "toolCalls": [{"name": "edit_file", "args": {"file_path": "util.go"}}]}
   716→  ]
   717→}`
   718→		if err := os.WriteFile(transcriptPath, []byte(transcriptContent), 0o644); err != nil {
   719→			t.Fatalf("failed to write transcript: %v", err)
   720→		}
   721→
   722→		ag, _ := agent.Get("gemini")
   723→		session, err := ag.ReadSession(&agent.HookInput{
   724→			SessionID:  "test-session",
   725→			SessionRef: transcriptPath,
   726→		})
   727→		if err != nil {
   728→			t.Fatalf("ReadSession() error = %v", err)
   729→		}
   730→
   731→		// Verify session metadata
   732→		if session.SessionID != "test-session" {
   733→			t.Errorf("SessionID = %q, want %q", session.SessionID, "test-session")
   734→		}
   735→		if session.AgentName != "gemini" {
   736→			t.Errorf("AgentName = %q, want %q", session.AgentName, "gemini")
   737→		}
   738→
   739→		// Verify NativeData is populated
   740→		if len(session.NativeData) == 0 {
   741→			t.Error("NativeData is empty, want transcript content")
   742→		}
   743→
   744→		// Verify ModifiedFiles computed
   745→		if len(session.ModifiedFiles) != 2 {
   746→			t.Errorf("ModifiedFiles = %v, want 2 files (main.go, util.go)", session.ModifiedFiles)
   747→		}
   748→	})
   749→
   750→	t.Run("WriteSession writes NativeData to file", func(t *testing.T) {
   751→		t.Parallel()
   752→		env := NewTestEnv(t)
   753→		env.InitRepo()
   754→
   755→		ag, _ := agent.Get("gemini")
   756→
   757→		// First read a session
   758→		srcPath := filepath.Join(env.RepoDir, "src.json")
   759→		srcContent := `{"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hello"}]}`
   760→		if err := os.WriteFile(srcPath, []byte(srcContent), 0o644); err != nil {
   761→			t.Fatalf("failed to write source: %v", err)
   762→		}
   763→
   764→		session, _ := ag.ReadSession(&agent.HookInput{
   765→			SessionID:  "test",
   766→			SessionRef: srcPath,
   767→		})
   768→
   769→		// Write to a new location
   770→		dstPath := filepath.Join(env.RepoDir, "dst.json")
   771→		session.SessionRef = dstPath
   772→
   773→		if err := ag.WriteSession(session); err != nil {
   774→			t.Fatalf("WriteSession() error = %v", err)
   775→		}
   776→
   777→		// Verify file was written
   778→		data, err := os.ReadFile(dstPath)
   779→		if err != nil {
   780→			t.Fatalf("failed to read destination: %v", err)
   781→		}
   782→		if string(data) != srcContent {
   783→			t.Errorf("written content = %q, want %q", string(data), srcContent)
   784→		}
   785→	})
   786→
   787→	t.Run("WriteSession rejects wrong agent", func(t *testing.T) {
   788→		t.Parallel()
   789→
   790→		ag, _ := agent.Get("gemini")
   791→
   792→		session := &agent.AgentSession{
   793→			SessionID:  "test",
   794→			AgentName:  "other-agent", // Wrong agent
   795→			SessionRef: "/tmp/test.json",
   796→			NativeData: []byte("data"),
   797→		}
   798→
   799→		err := ag.WriteSession(session)
   800→		if err == nil {
   801→			t.Error("WriteSession() should reject session from different agent")
   802→		}
   803→	})
   804→}

> AGENT

Now I see the problem. The test runs against the **real CLI repo** (not a test repo), and:

1. `runExplainBranchWithFilter` calls `getBranchCheckpoints` which calls `getReachableTemporaryCheckpoints`
2. That iterates over **all shadow branches** in this repo (including `entire/674d766-e3b0c4` and others)
3. For each shadow branch checkpoint, `convertTemporaryCheckpoint` calls `hasCodeChanges`
4. `hasCodeChanges` does `parentTree.Diff(commitTree)` using go-git's merkletrie

The shadow branch commits contain **the entire repo's working tree** (all files copied into the shadow branch). Diffing two full trees of this repo with go-git's merkletrie is extremely slow — that's where the 10-minute timeout comes from.

The test shouldn't be running against the real repo. It either needs a small isolated test repo, or it should be structured to only test the routing logic (which is all the test comment says it's doing) without actually calling the full `runExplain` pipeline.
